item.title: AKRON MARATHON ANNOUNCES BLUE LINE STRIDERS TRAINING SERIES IN PARTNERSHIP WITH SUMMACARE AND SUMMA HEALTH
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded: Akron, OH (May 19, 2021) — The Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health is thrilled to announce its Blue Line Striders training series in partnership with SummaCare, giving its running community a sneak peek into the new FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay course. During the Blue Line Striders training runs, happening once a month leading up to race day, participants will have the opportunity to run different sections of the Akron Marathon course. Additionally, each time runners meet, a doctor from Summa Health will join to discuss a health topic common for runners. All distances and paces are welcome! Each Blue Line Striders training run has been carefully chosen based on the training plans outlined by the Akron Marathon and is the perfect supplement to assist runners leading up to each race. Blue Line Striders training runs will begin at 7:00 a.m. and will preview sections of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon course: ● 4 miles: Sat., June 12, Relay Leg 1, 199 S. Broadway St, Akron, OH 44308 ● 7 miles: Sat., July 10, Relay Leg 2, 199 S. Broadway St, Akron, OH 44308 ● 7 miles: Sat., Aug. 21, Relay Leg 4, 1466 N. Portage Path, Akron, OH 44313 ● 12 or 20 miles: Sat., Sept. 4, 199 S. Broadway St, Akron, OH 44308 ● Runner’s Choice: Sat., Oct. 9, 499 Memorial Parkway, Akron, OH 44310 “As the new presenting sponsor of this year's Akron Marathon Race Series, Summa Health is actively making a deeper connection with our blue liners and supporting runners not only on race day, but throughout their training season in a meaningful way,” states Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon. “This program is their way to show its incredible level of support, and was designed to act as the perfect complement to the Akron Marathon training calendar.” Topics discussed by Summa Health physicians will include common spring/summer injuries, the importance of long runs, the importance of cross-training/core work/stretching, personal record tips, avoiding the wall, and post-race recovery. “We are thrilled to bring the expertise of our physicians to those participating in the Blue Line Striders Training Series,” said Dr. Nilesh Shah, Summa Health Sports Medicine Medical Director. “We know physical activity can sometimes come with injuries. By having these discussions, we hope to foster a safe and fun running environment for all, regardless of pace or experience.” To register or for more information on the Blue Line Striders events, please visit facebook.com/runAkron. The following race dates are confirmed: ● National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile, June 26, 2021 ● Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k, Aug. 14, 2021 ● FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay, Sept. 25, 2021 # # # About the Akron Marathon Race Series The Akron Marathon Race Series is organized by the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, a nonprofit group founded in 2002 to provide a world-class marathon and other events that promote health and fitness, stimulate the local economy, galvanize the community and benefit charitable organizations. The series features race dates in June (National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile) and August (Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k), culminating with the 19th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, Team Relay & Kids Fun Run in September. Additional information is available at AkronMarathon.org or by calling (330) 434-2RUN (2786). About Summa Health Summa Health is one of the largest integrated healthcare delivery systems in Ohio. Encompassing a network of hospitals, community medical centers, a health plan, an accountable care organization, a multi-specialty physician organization, research and the Summa Health Foundation, we are nationally renowned for excellence in patient care and for exceptional approaches to healthcare delivery. Summa’s clinical services are consistently recognized by the American Nurses Credentialing Center (Magnet status), U.S. News and World Report, Healthgrades, Thomson Reuters and The Leapfrog Group. For more information, visit summahealth.org or find us on Facebook at facebook.com/summahealth, Twitter, twitter.com/summahealth and LinkedIn linkedin.com/company/summahealth. About SummaCare SummaCare is a provider-owned regional health insurance company founded in 1993 in Akron, Ohio. SummaCare offers health insurance plans for employer groups and individuals. Its Medicare Advantage plans have been offered since 1996, and include medical and prescription drug (Part D) coverage and have an extensive network of more than 10,000 providers and 63 hospitals, including Summa Health. For more information, go to www.summacare.com.

item.title: 2021 AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES PRESENTED BY SUMMA HEALTH SET TO KICK OFF JUNE 26
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
Akron, OH (June 17, 2021) — For the sixth year, the Akron Marathon Race Series is excited to welcome runners beginning their summer racing journeys during the National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile on Sat., June 26, 2021, at 7:30 a.m. This year, its team is also thrilled to be joined by Summa Health as the presenting sponsor of its series. The Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health continues its goal of encouraging participation of all fitness levels. As a three-event race series with distances ranging from one mile to a full marathon, runners are encouraged to choose the series distances that suit their personal goals. With new guidance from both the CDC and the state of Ohio in place, the Akron Marathon has updated its Operational & Safety Guidelines to expand capacity, update mask guidelines, welcome spectators and host its traditional finisher festival. 2021 event changes:
  • If you are fully vaccinated, wearing a mask is optional.
  • Attendees who are not fully vaccinated should continue to wear face coverings throughout race areas unless actively running, eating, or drinking.
  • Certain services have been suspended including gear check and pace teams.
  • Both virtual and in-person races are available for all events.
  • The race will start with 10 separate waves, with runners from National Interstate leading each wave. There will be 200 participants per wave, and each wave will take approximately 45 seconds to start.
    • Each wave will be walked up to the start line, be held for 45 seconds, and have their own starting commands.
“While it is exciting to return to a sense of normalcy at our events and welcome a deeper partnership with Summa Health, the health and safety of our participants and volunteers remain our top priority,” Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon. “We will move forward with a hybrid approach, keeping several mitigation strategies in place and encouraging everyone who attends our events to be mindful and respectful of others’ personal space.” The National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile course highlights The University of Akron’s campus with a unique tour of downtown Akron including the new Main Street. Although it is designed for speed, the course supports both runners and walkers on their way to the finish on Summa Field inside InfoCision Stadium. “National Interstate Insurance has been a proud supporter of the Akron Marathon Race Series for several years,” stated Tony Prinzo, AVP, human resources at National Interstate Insurance Company. “This year is extra rewarding as we emerge from the pandemic and are able to enjoy the sense of community that the race series creates.  It is always exciting for us on race day and we look forward to spending this year’s 8k and 1 Mile reconnecting with the community and enjoying a great day of festivities.” The 8k and 1 Mile race will start at the intersection of Union Street and Exchange Street at 7:30 a.m. Optimal points for viewing runners can be found in the following locations:
  • Outside the InfoCision Stadium on Brown Street.
  • After the start, walk one block east to Spicer Street to see the runners at Mile 1.
  • From Spicer, head back towards the Start Line and utilize Gate 1 to enter the stadium
“We are extremely excited to be the presenting sponsor for the 2021 Akron Marathon Race Series and for the upcoming National Interstate 8k and 1 Mile kickoff event,” said Dr. Cliff Deveny, Summa Health president and CEO. “Getting back to a sense of normalcy, while continuing to practice all necessary safety measures, is an important step for our community. I thank the event organizers for their thoughtfulness in designing a safe event and I wish all participants the very best throughout the entire series.” The following race dates are confirmed: Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k, Aug. 14, 2021, and FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay, Sept. 25, 2021. For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, please visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: 2021 AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES PRESENTED BY SUMMA HEALTH KICKS OFF WITH A RECORD-BREAKING FEMALE 8K WIN
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
Akron, OH (June 26, 2021) — Nick Stricklen from Akron and Becki Spellman from Galloway were the respective 8k winners in the men’s and women’s races at the National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile, the first race of the 2021 Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health on Sat., June 26, 2021, beginning at 7:30 a.m. Spellman, a University of Akron track and field alumni, previously held the 8k women’s course record of 29:30 from 2017, and today, she set a new course record with a time of 29:24. As a longtime Akron Marathon athlete, in 2011 and 2016, she won the women’s Full Marathon and in 2018, she won the women’s Half Marathon. The National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile welcomed 1,761 in-person athletes and 106 virtual athletes for a total of 1,867 participants from 10 states, with ages 3 to 79 competing. The race began by highlighting The University of Akron’s campus with a unique tour of downtown Akron. Although it was designed for speed, the course supported both runners and walkers as they made their way to the finish on the Summa Field inside InfoCision Stadium. The morning’s first to cross the finish line in the 1 Mile race was Kevin Messick from Wadsworth and Renee Harden from Medina. National Interstate Insurance, in its sixth year as Presenting Sponsor for this first race in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, had 37 employees participating in the race. “Today, we were proud to bring our team together for the National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile race,” states Tony Prinzo, AVP, Human Resources of National Interstate Insurance. “We take a great deal of pride in supporting the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. This year feels extra special as we were able to come together in person and feel a sense of community with volunteers, runners and staff all doing something good for their social and physical well-being.” The day’s winners included: Men’s 8k:
  1. Nick Stricklen, Akron, 25:45
  2. Hunter Heaton, Copley, 25:51
  3. Dylan Garritano, Akron, 26:18

item.title: AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES PRESENTED BY SUMMA HEALTH CONTINUES WITH SOLD OUT GOODYEAR HALF MARATHON AND SOLD OUT FIRSTENERGY AKRON MARATHON
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
Akron, OH (July 13, 2021) — After a successful kickoff to the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health during the National Interstate 8k &1 Mile in June, the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is thrilled to announce sellouts in the Goodyear Half Marathon on Aug. 14, 2021, as well as the FirstEnergy Full Marathon on Sept. 25, 2021.

For the Aug. 14 Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k, limited spots are available in the 10k; and for the marquee event on Sept. 25, limited spots remain in the Half Marathon and Relay events.

“We’re seeing incredible participation numbers,” shared Anne Bitong, president of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “With unparalleled organization on-course and off, the best volunteers, and amazing spectators ready to cheer on the runners, we’re ready to deliver unforgettable racing experiences and are so excited to be back!

The Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k is the second event in the series, and participants will travel through Akron’s East End, explore Goodyear’s campus, and take a lap around the test track at the closed-to-the-public Akron Proving Grounds before their finish under the skywalk at Goodyear’s Global Headquarters.

During the marquee race and final event of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay runners will follow the blue line through 11 Akron neighborhoods, beginning in downtown Akron next to the Akron Art Museum and, for the first time, ending at downtown Akron’s Lock 3.

For more information or volunteer opportunities for the remaining two race series events and race registration for the final event, visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: WINNERS ANNOUNCED IN THE SOLD-OUT GOODYEAR HALF MARATHON & RECORD-BREAKING 10K
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded: Akron, OH (Aug. 16, 2021) — More than 2,000 athletes gathered at Goodyear Global Headquarters for the second race in the 7th annual Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, with a recording-breaking race in the men’s overall 10k. At the sold-out Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k, Aiman Scullion from Akron and Catherine Joecken from Bay Village were the respective winners in the men’s and women’s Goodyear Half Marathon, finishing at 1:09:07 and 1:24:50. The men’s 10k title was taken by Antonio Cardona Rodriguez from Puerto Rico, beating the previous 10k record of 33:14 with a time of 31:09, and the women’s 10k winner, Paola Ramos Lugo from Puerto Rico, finished with a time of 36:07. The Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k welcomed runners ages 12-85 competing on Sat., Aug. 14, 2021, beginning at 6:30 a.m. This year, the Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k hosted a hybrid approach to its second race in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health keeping several mitigation strategies in place to ensure the safety of all runners, including all participants completing a COVID-19 questionnaire 72 hours before the race. Additionally, 200 runners at a time began socially distant and in five separate waves for the Half Marathon and in eight separate waves for the 10k— each spaced three minutes apart as part of the teams’ COVID Operational & Safety Guidelines. “We’re incredibly grateful for the athletes, volunteers, partners, and spectators that filled the sold-out Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k, and we share our deep appreciation for their flexibility and cooperation in support of the new health and safety measures at this iconic race,” stated Anne Bitong, President & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company, in its seventh year as presenting sponsor for this second race in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, provided support with more than 140 Goodyear associates, who laced up to run or volunteered at the day’s event. Since the Marathon’s inception, Summa Health has proudly supported medical aid stations across its events. This year, the Summa Health team made the transition to presenting sponsor of the entire Akron Marathon Race Series, as well as continuing to run vital aid stations for runners. As stated by Cliff Deveny, M.D., the president and CEO of Summa Health, “Giving back to the community is one of the most important things that we do.” Dr. Deveny also participated in the 10k. item.title: AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES PRESENTED BY SUMMA HEALTH CONTINUES WITH PROOF OF VACCINATION OR NEGATIVE COVID-19 TEST REQUIREMENTS
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded: Akron, OH (Aug. 26, 2021) — After two successful events in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation has announced its marquee event, the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay on Sept. 25, 2021, will now require runners and volunteers to be fully vaccinated (with proof of a COVID-19 vaccination card) or have a negative COVID-19 test result 72 hours before the race to participate. This protocol was updated to help protect the health and safety of the public in light of the increase in COVID-19 cases and is aligned with best practices for mass gatherings.  As always, Summa Health, the Akron Marathon, and FirstEnergy event organizers are working closely with the City of Akron and Summit County Public Health on race weekend plans that align with Summit County’s public health and safety efforts to protect its runners, volunteers, and spectators. Due to the increasing COVID-19 numbers and the Delta variant, new health requirements were added.  “In order to ensure the race experience that our runners expect—including the Finisher’s Festival—we have to make certain of their safety first and foremost,” states Anne Bitong, president of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “I want to express my gratitude for our team, the City of Akron, and Summit County, along with our sponsors and volunteers who have been working together on the detailed logistics of the event. Health and safety at all levels have been discussed—from packet pick-up and fluid stations to wave starts and lowered capacity—helping to keep our runners feeling safe and together. That’s what this community has always been about.” During the Aug. Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k, 81 percent of runners self-identified as fully vaccinated. For the Sept. events, proof of vaccination may be presented as a hard copy, photocopy, or digital version of an immunization record. Registered runners who are not fully vaccinated must provide a negative COVID-19 test result for a test administered within 72 hours of attending the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay. Proof of vaccination or negative COVID-19 test will be required to pick up an in-person race bib at the Akron Marathon Health & Fitness Expo on Friday, Sept. 24. The Akron Marathon defines “fully vaccinated” as individuals who are two weeks after their second dose in a two-dose vaccine series or two weeks after a single-dose vaccine. “The health and safety of our community is our top priority,” states Mike Bernstein, system director, corporate communications of Summa Health. “We strongly recommend the available COVID vaccines and commend the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation for its work in keeping race participants safe.” The FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay, which will follow the Blue Line through the streets of Akron on Sept. 25., is the third and final race in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. “FirstEnergy applauds the race organizers and local officials who are keeping the health and safety of race participants, their supporters and volunteers at the forefront to ensure a safe and successful event,” said Steven Strah, president and chief executive officer of FirstEnergy. “As the proud title sponsor of this marquee Akron event, FirstEnergy and its employees look forward to celebrating with the runners when they cross the finish line in September.”    Need to find a vaccine near you? Contact your local physician or visit vaccinefinder.org for more information on COVID-19 vaccines and where to find one.  Based on national standards, accepted COVID-19 tests are those that have received FDA emergency use authorization and also include RT-PCR, RT-LAMP, lateral flow, and antigen tests.  For more information or volunteer opportunities and race registration for the final event, visit AkronMarathon.org. # # #  About the Akron Marathon Race Series The Akron Marathon Race Series is organized by the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, a non-profit group founded in 2002 to provide a world-class marathon and other events that promote health and fitness, stimulate the local economy, galvanize the community and benefit charitable organizations. The series features race dates in June (National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile) and August (Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k), culminating with the 19th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, Team Relay & Kids Fun Run in September. Additional information is available at AkronMarathon.org or by calling (330) 434-2RUN (2786). For:                 IMMEDIATE RELEASE August 26, 2021 Contact:         Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation Kat Allen, kat@ampstrategy.com 330-714-2274

item.title: AKRON MARATHON ANNOUNCES CIRCLE K DONATION TO ITS RUNNERSHIP PROGRAM
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
[et_pb_section fb_built="1" admin_label="section" _builder_version="3.22"][et_pb_row admin_label="row" _builder_version="3.25" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat"][et_pb_column type="4_4" _builder_version="3.25" custom_padding="|||" custom_padding__hover="|||"][et_pb_text admin_label="Text" _builder_version="4.7.7" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat" hover_enabled="0" sticky_enabled="0"]

Akron, OH (Sept. 7, 2021) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is thrilled to announce Circle K, one of its Gold Level Sponsors, has donated 60 race entries to the organization’s Blue Line Runnership Program that provides free race entries to local nonprofits and their clients.

Part of the mission of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is to benefit nonprofit and charitable organizations. To date, more than $6 million dollars has been raised through the net proceeds of events, runner donations, and its Blue Line Charity Partner Program.

Specifically, the Runnership Program offers runner scholarships/race entries to area nonprofits that serve the underprivileged, disadvantaged, or those struggling with mental health and/or recovery. Applications will be accepted through Sept. 14 at akronmarathon.org/runnership.

If chosen, free race entries will be awarded based on their organization’s services and eligibility. These individuals will be able to participate in the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay, Sept. 25, 2021.

Circle K is one of the largest convenience store brands in the United States and is a wholly owned subsidiary of Alimentation Couche-Tard. In Summit County, we have 61 stores, and they’ve proudly been part of the Akron Marathon since 2018.

“Running is a hobby of mine, and Akron Marathon gives me the opportunity to couple that with giving back to our community,” said Jack Wiolland of Circle K. “We worked as a team to not only participate in the relay but to create excitement to raise money for our community. Through our Annual Charity Golf Outing, held every August, and collections in local stores, we are committed to reinvest in our region.”

“As a nonprofit ourselves, we understand the work and dedication that goes into providing services to our community,” states Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “We’re so proud of this donation by Circle K, the Runnership Program, and the opportunities to partner with incredible nonprofits on the Blue Line.”

For more information, race registration, and volunteer opportunities, please visit AkronMarathon.org.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

item.title: COUNTDOWN TO THE AKRON MARATHON HAS OFFICIALLY BEGUN FOR RUNNERS AND SPECTATORS
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
Akron, OH (Sept. 17, 2021) — Excitement and preparations are building for one of Akron’s largest sporting events of the year, the marquee event of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay is set for Sat., Sept. 25, 2021. The new course, built for safety and designed to be a foot-tour of Akron’s well-known landmarks, highlights North Hill, The University of Akron, Firestone Park, the Ohio Erie Canalway Towpath Trail, Sand Run Metro Park, and West Akron. The course supports both runners and walkers on their way to the finish in downtown Akron—where a world-class finish inside Lock 3 and the popular Finisher Festival awaits them. The FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay will see more than 7,000 participants, even more spectators, and this year thanks to a partnership with ArtsNow with a grant funded by the Ohio Arts Council, new art entrepreneurs into the city. “We’re creating a world-class running experience for our participants, and our spectators help us set that stage as a vital part of amplifying our race atmosphere in Akron,” states Anne Bitong, President & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “Whether you join us in support of one particular runner, or are there to cheer everyone on, we’re looking forward to seeing you along the Blue Line!” Here are ways to safely spectate in each of Akron’s five neighborhoods: Please be mindful of those around you and keep a 6-foot distance between you and other spectator groups. If you are fully vaccinated, wearing a mask is optional. Attendees who are not fully vaccinated should continue to wear face coverings throughout race areas unless actively running, eating, or drinking. Downtown Akron, Start Line, Miles 4, 5, 11, 12, and the Finish Line *The Finish Line will be live-streamed on the Akron Marathon’s Facebook page! First Runner: 7:00 a.m. Last Runner: 2:00 p.m. Watch the start of the race north of the starting line on Broadway between Market and MLK Walk south using High St. towards Mile 4 (corner of High St. and Bowery St). Remain on High St. to see runners nearing Mile 12. Walk one block west to Main and Bowery to see runners as they approach the finish. *Spectators are not allowed inside Lock 3 for the runner-only Finisher Festival. North Hill, Miles 1, 2, and 3 First Runner: 7:04 a.m. Last Runner: 8:10 a.m. Cheer on the runners by lining S. Main St. to watch runners at Mile 1 and again at Mile 3 just north of the All-American Bridge. Firestone Park, Miles 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 First Runner: 7:28 a.m. Last Runner: 10:00 a.m. Cheer on the runners at Firestone Park at Mile 7 or at Mile 9 near Firestone Stadium. Merriman Valley, Miles 16 and 17 First Runner: 8:15 a.m. Last Runner: 11:40 a.m. Runners will be exiting the Ohio & Erie Canal Towpath Trail at Portage Path at Mile 16.5 on their approach to Mile 17 at Sand Run Metro Park. Northwest Akron, Miles 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, and 25 First Runner: 8:36 a.m. Last Runner: 1:40 p.m. Cheer on the runners by lining the West Akron neighborhood during the runners’ most challenging miles. Road closures will occur in each area during the active first-runner/last-runner times listed above. View Akron Marathon Road Closures for an extensive list and plan ahead! If you live along the Blue Line and are interested in hosting an official Blue Line Block Party, the Akron Marathon will provide you a block party kit with festive items and noisemakers while supplies last to get the party started. If you are interested in hosting a Blue Line block party, please connect with Katie Riley at kriley@akronmarathon.org. Or, looking to get more involved with the race? Volunteers are still needed: View available spots. For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health or volunteering, please visit AkronMarathon.org.

# # #

About the Akron Marathon Race Series The Akron Marathon Race Series is organized by the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, a nonprofit group founded in 2002 to provide a world-class marathon and other events that promote health and fitness, stimulate the local economy, galvanize the community and benefit charitable organizations. The series features race dates in June (National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile) and August (Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k), culminating with the 19th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, Team Relay & Kids Fun Run in September. Additional information is available at AkronMarathon.org or by calling (330) 434-2RUN (2786).

item.title: THOUSANDS RACE AND CELEBRATE DURING FINAL EVENT OF AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES PRESENTED BY SUMMA HEALTH
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded: Akron, OH (Sept. 25, 2021) — More than 6,000 athletes and thousands of spectators gathered safely at the marquee event of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay, which began with a new starting line at the Akron Art Museum. On a crisp and cool morning, the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay welcomed runners with ages 14 to 84 competing on Sat., Sept. 25, 2021, beginning at 7:00 a.m. Traveling 26.2 miles through the streets of Akron at 2:25:07 and 3:18:45 Nick Stricklen of Akron, and Teresa Ferguson of Coventry Township were the top finishers in today’s Marathon. The first runners to cross the finish line outside of Lock 3 in the Half Marathon distance were Jeremiah Fitzgerald of Lakewood and Becki Spellman of Galloway with times of 1:08:03 and 1:20:53. Dylan Garritano of Akron was the runner-up in the men’s Marathon with a time of 2:27:30, while Israel Merkle of Akron crossed the line third at 2:28:08 For the women’s Marathon, Greer Rothermel of Uniontown, finished second with a time of 3:20:10 followed by Taylor Warrick from Cleveland, 3:26:51 in the Marathon. (Complete winner information can be found at the end of this release.) In the Half Marathon, Nathaniel Orndorf from Akron and Josh Rieskamp from Columbus placed second and third in the men’s division. Caroline Ostry from Copley in second place and Brittany Eismon from Hudson in third place, rounded out the winner’s podium for the women’s Half Marathon. Top times in the Marathon’s Masters Division (40 years and older) were put up by Brian Polen from Wooster and overall female Marathon winner Teresa Ferguson from Coventry Township. For the Half Marathon, the top masters were David Stewart from Mogadore and Leslie Owen from Copley. “We loved being back with you, Akron!” said Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “To our Blue Line runners, sponsors, supporters, volunteers, and vendors, this community truly showed the best of itself during this unforgettable year. It is your commitment that helps make this a world-class event—and we’re so incredibly proud of your work and grateful for you! “Congratulations to all those who participated in this weekend’s events,” said Cliff Deveny, M.D., Summa Health president and CEO. “From running to walking and even cheering on your friends and family—we celebrate your hard work. We are honored to be part of this great organization and can’t wait for next year’s Akron Marathon.” Friday night, the Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children’s Hospital had more than 500 kids ages 12 and under race their own “big race” along the one-mile course and shared finish line. Plans are already underway for the 20th anniversary of the Akron Marathon which is set for Sept. 24, 2022, and details will continue to be updated at AkronMarathon.org in the months to come. List of winners in the Full Marathon: Female Overall: Teresa Ferguson, Coventry Township, 3:18:45 Greer Rothermel, Uniontown, 3:20:10 Taylor Warrick, Cleveland, 3:26:51   Male Overall: Nick Stricklen, Akron, 2:25:07 Dylan Garritano, Akron, 2:27:30 Israel Merkle, Akron, 2:28:08   Female Masters: Teresa Ferguson, Coventry Township, 3:18:45 Katie McNeil, Zanesville, 3:46:56 Jennie Swires, Mantua, 3:47:34   Male Masters: Brian Polen, Wooster, 2:42:44 Paul Stock, Hudson, 2:50:42 Ron Hayes, Akron, 2:57:40   List of winners in the Half Marathon: Female Overall: Becki Spellman, Galloway, 1:20:53 Caroline Ostry, Copley, 1:27:31 Brittany Eismon, Hudson, 1:28:20   Male Overall: Jeremiah Fitzgerald, Lakewood, 1:08:03 Nathaniel Orndorf, Akron, 1:09:34 Josh Rieskamp, Columbus, 1:09:49   Female Masters: Leslie Owen, Copley, 1:37:37 Nicole Gareri-David, Canton, 1:37:40 Tammie Pruett, Massillon, 1:44:14   Male Masters: David Stewart, Mogadore, 1:25:21 Mark Rohrer, Wadsworth, 1:27:56 Jason Vickers, Massillon, 1:28:06   For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, please visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: AKRON MARATHON CHARITABLE CORPORATION ANNOUNCES SUCCESS OF BLUE LINE CHARITY PROGRAM
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
[et_pb_section fb_built="1" admin_label="section" _builder_version="3.22"][et_pb_row admin_label="row" _builder_version="3.25" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat"][et_pb_column type="4_4" _builder_version="3.25" custom_padding="|||" custom_padding__hover="|||"][et_pb_text admin_label="Text" _builder_version="4.7.7" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat" hover_enabled="0" sticky_enabled="0"]

Akron, OH (Dec. 28, 2021) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation staff and Board of Directors are thrilled to announce its nonprofit charity partners through its Blue Line Charity Program raised $94,310.00 during the 2021 racing season, a 9.53 percent increase from 2019.

Part of the mission of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is to benefit nonprofit and charitable organizations. To date, more than $6 million has been raised through the net proceeds of events, runner donations, and its Blue Line Charity Partner Program.

The Blue Line Charity Partner Program allows nonprofits from the community to use the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health as a fundraiser. With over 14,000 runners and 2,000 volunteers, the Akron Marathon and related events provide a large audience for nonprofit organizations.

Local nonprofit organizations with a 501(c)3 status are eligible to apply and the top charities that raise more than $5,000 as part of the Blue Line Charity Program will receive a donation from the Akron Marathon. Donations vary depending on annual proceeds.

2021 Top Fundraisers include:

  • Craine’s Cholangiocarcinoma Crew: $39,193 (+ $5,000 donated by Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation)
  • Akron Children’s Hospital: $16,005 (+ $2,000 donated by Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation)
  • Melina Michelle Edenfield Foundation: $7,390 (+ $1,000 donated by Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation)

Additional charity partners include:

  • Akron-Canton Regional Foodbank
  • American Heart Association - Akron Heart Walk
  • Building for Tomorrow
  • Curated Storefront
  • Family Promise of Summit County
  • Girls on the Run of Northeast Ohio
  • Golden Treasures Golden Retriever Rescue
  • Hope and Healing Survivor Resource Center (Battered Women's Shelter and Rape Crisis Center of Summit & Medina Counties)
  • International Welcome Center
  • Open Arms Adoption
  • Rahab Ministries
  • Running2BWell
  • Stewart’s Caring Place
  • Summa Health
  • Wellington Exempted Village Schools District

As part of this program, nonprofit partners are asked to recruit runners who will fundraise on their behalf, as well as volunteers to give their time on race weekend. All funds raised by the individual nonprofits will go directly to them.

“We’re thrilled with the results of this year’s Blue Line Charity Program and grateful for our running community who showed such support to our nonprofit partners,” states Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “As a nonprofit, we know the work and dedication that goes into providing services to Northeast Ohio and these numbers reflect our passion and mission to benefit nonprofit and charitable organizations.”

Applications for the 2022 Blue Line Charity Program are now open. Apply Here.

# # #

Contact:

Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation

Kat Allen, kat@ampstrategy.com

330-714-2274

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

item.title: AKRON MARATHON ANNOUNCES ALL PRESENTING SPONSORS OF RACE SERIES EVENTS RETURN IN 2022 AND OPENING REGISTRATION OF 20TH MARQUEE EVENT
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
[et_pb_section fb_built="1" admin_label="section" _builder_version="3.22"][et_pb_row admin_label="row" _builder_version="3.25" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat"][et_pb_column type="4_4" _builder_version="3.25" custom_padding="|||" custom_padding__hover="|||"][et_pb_text admin_label="Text" _builder_version="4.7.7" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat" hover_enabled="0" sticky_enabled="0"]

Public registration of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health is set to open on Jan. 20, 2022.

Akron, OH (Jan. 11, 2022) - The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation announced today that FirstEnergy Corp., The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company, and National Interstate Insurance Company have once again pledged their continued support through 2024 for the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health.

The Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health was designed to encourage participation for all fitness levels. With distances ranging from 1-mile to the marathon, runners pick the series combination that suits their goals.

“Strong partners are the foundation to the success of the world-class race series we’re able to host,” says Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon. “We’re incredibly grateful for the continued partnerships and friendships of these community-centered Northeast Ohio organizations.”

Additionally in 2022, the Akron Marathon team will celebrate the 20th running of its FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay. With an updated logo, monthly celebrations, 20th celebration running gear, and events, the year will be filled with honoring those who have been involved throughout the years. Celebration plans are underway and being finalized by an active committee and Board of Directors.

Confirmed Race Dates for 2022:

NATIONAL INTERSTATE 8K & 1 MILE: June 24 & 25 2022: Kick off the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health with the National Interstate 1 Mile on Friday night! The 8k will be held on Saturday, and the course highlights The University of Akron’s campus with a unique tour of downtown Akron.

GOODYEAR HALF MARATHON & 10K: August 13, 2022: The Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k brings the iconic landmarks of Goodyear right under your feet for a unique and unforgettable racing experience. item.title: AKRON MARATHON ANNOUNCES BLUE JEAN BASH TO CELEBRATE 20 YEARS ON THE BLUE LINE
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
[et_pb_section fb_built="1" admin_label="section" _builder_version="3.22"][et_pb_row admin_label="row" _builder_version="3.25" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat"][et_pb_column type="4_4" _builder_version="3.25" custom_padding="|||" custom_padding__hover="|||"][et_pb_text admin_label="Text" _builder_version="4.7.7" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat" hover_enabled="0" sticky_enabled="0"]

Akron, OH (March 21, 2022) - The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation announced today it will host its Blue Jean Bash on Sept. 22, 2022, to celebrate the 20th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay.

During the event, the John S. Knight Center will be transformed into a 20-year celebration, filled with interactive displays, running celebrities, live entertainment, and a walk down the history of the Blue Line. Honorary Chairs of the Blue Jean Bash include City of Akron Mayor Horrigan, Summit County Executive Shapiro, and Summa Health’s Dr. Shah.

The Blue Jean Bash will be the largest fundraiser for the Akron Marathon and hosted by Steve and Jeannine Marks, race co-founders, whose family also serves as the presenting sponsor. Thanks to the generosity of donors, from events like this, the Akron Marathon can continue to improve health and wellness in Northeast Ohio. Through the Akron Marathon’s 20-year history,
the organization has:

  • Celebrated 170,529 Blue Line Finishers
  • Raised over $6 million for charity
  • Generated $133 million of economic impact to the Greater Akron area
  • Provided 13,604 complimentary race entries
  • Accumulated over 132,740 volunteer hours

Tickets and sponsorship to the Blue Jean Bash will help reach the Finish Line towards the organization’s $400,000 fundraising goal. For more information on tickets and sponsorships, please visit AkronMarathon.org/BlueJeanBash.

# # #

About the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation
The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is a nonprofit group founded in 2002 to provide a world-class marathon and other
events that promote health and fitness, stimulate the local economy, galvanize the community and benefit charitable organizations.
It organizes the Akron Marathon Race Series that features race dates in June (National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile) and August
(Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k), culminating with the 20th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, Team Relay
& Kids Fun Run in September. Additional information is available at AkronMarathon.org or by calling (330) 434-2RUN (2786)

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

item.title: AKRON MARATHON ANNOUNCES KICKOFF TO TRAINING FOR UPCOMING RACE SERIES
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON MARATHON ANNOUNCES KICKOFF TO TRAINING FOR UPCOMING RACE SERIES

Registration prices for all events are set to increase on June 1, 2022

AKRON, Ohio (May 23, 2022) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is thrilled to announce the kickoff to the 18-week training program of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. Detailed training plans with beginner and competitive options begin Mon., May 23, 2022. Crafted to include each event in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, training plans are the perfect supplement to assist runners in completing their daily runs leading up to each race. Training plans can be found at AkronMarathon.org/training. Now is the time to commit to running the Race Series by registering before prices increase on Wed., June 1, 2022. Anyone that is registered for all three races through June 20 will be entered into a drawing to win one of 20 pairs of Brooks Launch running shoes in partnership with Second Sole Akrun in honor of the 20-year celebration of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, and Team Relay. In addition to all the runner premiums received from the individual races, runners participating in all three events of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health (who are registered for all three races by June 20) will:
  • Earn a special race series medal after completing all three events.
  • Be rewarded with a commemorative race series medal rack
The Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health was designed to encourage participation for all fitness levels. With distances ranging from 1 mile to the marathon, pick the series combination that suits your goals. Running the series will be easy as you follow a typical training calendar to benchmark your way to our marquee September event. The race series kicks off on Friday, June 24 with the 1 mile, followed on Saturday, June 25 by the National Interstate 8k. The Goodyear Half Marathon and 10k are set for Aug. 13, 2022, and the marquee event — the 20th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, and Team Relay — will follow the Blue Line through the streets of Akron on Sept. 24, 2022. For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, including race registration and volunteer opportunities, please visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: 2022 AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES PRESENTED BY SUMMA HEALTH SET TO KICK OFF JUNE 24 WITH NEW FRIDAY NIGHT MILE; VOLUNTEERS STILL NEEDED
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, Ohio (June 16, 2022) — For the seventh year, the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health is excited to welcome runners beginning their summer racing journeys during the National Interstate new Friday evening 1 Mile on June 24, 2022, at 7 p.m. and the 8k on Saturday, June 25, 2022, at 7:30 a.m.  The Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health continues its goal of encouraging participation of all fitness levels. As a three-event race series with distances ranging from 1 mile to a full marathon, runners are encouraged to choose the series distances that suit their personal goals.  This year, the 8k & 1 Mile course will feature a new Friday evening 1 Mile, a new start line on Spicer St., a block away from The University of Akron’s InfoCision Stadium, a new finish line on Carroll St., Finishers Festival inside Coleman Commons, and updated 8k and 1 Mile courses. Changes to the race are due to The University of Akron’s recent announcement that it will be replacing the turf field at InfoCision Stadium - Summa Field, which will impact race day.  The 1 Mile on Friday, June 24, 2022, begins at 7 p.m. and on Saturday, June 25, 2022,  the 8k begins at 7:30 a.m., with registration closing for each event on Monday, June 20, 2022.  The National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile course highlights The University of Akron’s campus with a unique tour of downtown Akron, including the new Main Street. Although it is designed for speed, the course supports both runners and walkers on their way to the finish line. “We are honored to continue our relationship with the Akron Marathon Race Series,” said   Tony Prinzo, vice president of human resources, National Interstate. “It is exciting to see our race weekend evolve, and also to serve as the kick-off to the entire series.  As I see our community come together for each race, I am proud of our community for creating opportunities for wellness, volunteerism, and celebration.” Optimal points & tips for viewing runners:
  • Spectators can watch runners start on Spicer St., just outside InfoCision Stadium. After the start, make your way to through Coleman Commons to the finish line on Carroll St., just beyond the Student Union
  • For the 1 Mile, spectators wishing to see the finish may need to head to the finish line prior to the race start, as it is a half-mile away.
  • Runners & spectators should choose a meeting location prior to the race start to meet up after the race. 
”We’re excited for another year of events and our ongoing partnership with the Akron Marathon Race Series,” said Dr. Cliff Deveny, Summa Health president and CEO. “Congratulations to the event organizers and best of luck to all of this year’s participants.” Volunteer opportunities are still available for June 24 and 25 events as well as all race series events and can be found at AkronMarathon.org/volunteer. As a volunteer for the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, individuals and groups have the opportunity to make a significant contribution to the Greater Akron community, meet new people, share skills and talents, and help make races successful world-class events for runners, their families, spectators and for the City of Akron. We are looking for groups as well as individuals to help make our events a success.  If you would like additional information on volunteering, please email Katie Riley, Community Outreach Director, or call the marathon office at (330) 434-2786. The Goodyear Half Marathon and 10k is set for Aug. 13, 2022, and the marquee event — the 20th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, and Team Relay — will follow the Blue Line through the streets of Akron on Sept. 24, 2022. For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, please visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: 2022 AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES PRESENTED BY SUMMA HEALTH KICKS OFF WITH NEW EVENT RECORDS IN THE MEN’S AND WOMEN’S 1 MILE RACE
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, Ohio (June 25, 2022) — Dylan Garritano from Akron and Becki Spellman from Galloway were the respective 8k winners in the men’s and women’s races at the National Interstate 8k, the first race of the 2022 Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health on Sat., June 25, 2022. On Friday evening, June 24, 2022, the first to cross the finish line in the 1 Mile race was Jacob Ondash from Akron with a time of 4:25 and Shelby Nolan from Toledo with a time of 5:04— both setting new event records. The race began by highlighting The University of Akron’s campus with a unique tour of downtown Akron. Although it was designed for speed, the course supported both runners and walkers as they made their way to the finish in Colman Commons. With in-person and virtual options, the 8k welcomed 1,414 in-person participants and the 1 Mile had 290 participants. With the races on different days for the first time, 161 runners were able to participate in both races. National Interstate Insurance, in its seventh year as presenting sponsor for this first race in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, had more than 30 employees participating in the race, including Tony Prinzo, vice president of human resources for National Interstate, who participated in both the 1 Mile and 8k. “We are honored to continue our relationship with the Akron Marathon Race Series,” said Prinzo. “It is exciting to see our race weekend evolve, and also to serve as the kick-off to the entire series. As I see our region come together for each race, I am proud of our community for creating opportunities for wellness, volunteerism, and celebration.” The winners included: Men’s 8k:
  1. Dylan Garritano, Akron, 25:58
  2. Chris Fyock, Rocky River, 26:04
  3. Nick Marino, Stow, 26:15
Women’s 8k:
  1. Becki Spellman, Galloway, 29:41
  2. Jessi Bentley, Wadsworth, 31:01
  3. Brittany Eismon, Hudson, 31:34
Men’s Masters 8k:
  1. Paul Stock, Hudson, 29:39
  2. Mark Rohrer, Wadsworth, 30:55
  3. David Stewart, Mogadore, 30:56
Women’s Masters 8k:
  1. Teresa Ferguson, Akron, 34:26
  2. Leslie Owen, Copley, 35:00
  3. Danelle Villers, Copley, 35:29
Men’s 1 Mile:
  1. Jacob Ondash, Akron, 4:25—new event record! (The previous record was 4:31.)
  2. Nick Marino, Stow, 4:36
  3. Dylan Garritano, Akron, 4:37
Women’s 1 Mile:
  1. Shelby Nolan, Toledo, 5:04—new event record! (The previous record was 5:34.)
  2. Hannah Long, Akron, 5:06
  3. Becki Spellman, Galloway, 5:12
Men’s Masters 1 Mile:
  1. Rick Williamson, Hilliard, 5:20
  2. David Krause, Strongsville, 5:43
  3. Frank Chahulski, Strongsville, 5:47
Women’s Masters 1 Mile:
  1. Theresa Wright, Medina, 6:42
  2. Erin Lewis, Cleveland, 7:27
  3. Nikaeda Griffie, Akron, 7:38
“We were thrilled to welcome back runners this weekend and witnessed strong performances on both the 1 Mile and 8k courses that were faster and flatter for our participants,” Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation stated. “While today marks the kickoff of the Akron Race Series, it also marks the beginning of our 20-year celebration of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, and Team Relay—surely a year to remember!” Race registration and volunteer opportunities for the remaining two-race series events can be found at AkronMarathon.org. The Goodyear Half Marathon and 10k are set for Aug. 13, 2022, and the marquee event — the 20th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, and Team Relay — will follow the Blue Line through the streets of Akron on Sept. 24, 2022. For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, please visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: AKRON MARATHON CONFIRMS RUNNING CELEBRITIES ATTENDING 2022 BLUE JEAN BASH + HEALTH AND FITNESS EXPO
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded: Akron, OH (August 4, 2022) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation has confirmed its running celebrities to help celebrate the 20th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, and Team Relay at the Blue Jean Bash fundraiser on Thurs., Sept 22, 2022. Its running celebrities will also attend the Health & Fitness Expo set for Friday, Sept. 23, 2022. This year’s running celebrities are Ali Feller, Meb Keflezighi, Bill Rodgers, and Kathrine Switzer. Ali Feller is a blogger, freelance writer, editor, and host of the “Ali on the Run Show podcast.” In the podcast, Feller interviews runners about why they love the sport, how running makes them feel, and what they enjoy outside of running. The podcast is one of the top-running podcasts in the world and has more than 14.8 million downloads. Ali will be doing a live podcast from the Blue Line Celebration stage at the Health & Fitness Expo on Friday! Meb Keflezighi is the first runner in history to win the New York Marathon, the Boston Marathon, and an Olympic Medal. Keflezighi spends his free time training, competing, making personal appearances, and overseeing the MEB (Maintaining Excellent Balance) Foundation which promotes young health, education, and fitness.*The Akron Marathon’s Ambassador Award Recipient in 2016. Bill Rodgers is a four-time winner of the Boston and New York City marathons. Rodgers is also a member of the National Track & Field Hall of Fame, the National Distance Running Hall of Fame and is one of four American men to have medaled in the IAAF World Cross Country Championships, earning a bronze medal in 1975., *The Akron Marathon’s Ambassador Award Recipient in 2009.   Kathrine Switzer is an athlete, activist, and author best known for challenging the all-male tradition of the Boston Marathon and becoming the first woman to officially enter and run the event. Switzer created programs in 27 countries for more than 1 million women that led to the inclusion of the women’s marathon as an official event in the Olympic Games. *The Akron Marathon’s Ambassador Award Recipient in 2008. During the Blue Jean Bash, the John S. Knight Center will be transformed into a 20-year celebration, filled with interactive displays, running celebrities, live entertainment, and a walk down the history of the Blue Line. Honorary Chairs of the Blue Jean Bash include City of Akron Mayor Horrigan, Summit County Executive Shapiro, and Summa Health’s Dr. Shah. The Blue Jean Bash will be the largest fundraiser for the Akron Marathon and hosted by Steve and Jeannine Marks, race co-founders, whose family also serves as the presenting sponsor. Kick off race weekend with the Akron Marathon and celebrate 20 years along the Blue Line. Tickets and sponsorship to the Blue Jean Bash will help reach the Finish Line towards the organization’s $400,000 fundraising goal. For more information on tickets and sponsorships, please visit akronmarathon.org/bluejeanbash.

item.title: AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES PRESENTED BY SUMMA HEALTH CONTINUES ON AUG. 13 WITH GOODYEAR HALF MARATHON AND 10K
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
Akron, OH (August 8, 2022) — The Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health is excited to announce the race series will continue with its second event, the Goodyear Half Marathon and 10k on Aug. 13, 2022. During The Goodyear Half Marathon and 10k, participants will start with a lap around the Goodyear Test Track at the Akron Proving Grounds, and travel through Akron’s East End and Ellet neighborhoods, to cross the finish line under the skywalk at Goodyear’s Global Headquarters.
All Akron Marathon Race Series events end with their ever-popular Finisher Festivals, featuring a live band, local food favorites, and high-level swag—and The Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k will live up to those expectations with a variety of vendors and displays, including the Swenson’s Food Truck, Roll by Goodyear vehicle, and each runner receiving a premium short sleeve performance shirt and commemorative medal. For this race, Packet Pick-Up will be held on Fri., Aug. 12, 2022, from 11:00 am - 7:00 pm at Hilton Garden Inn Akron, where all runners must pick up their race packets. There will be no race day packet pick-up offered.
The Goodyear Half Marathon and 10k is the second race in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. As well as providing financial support for the race, this year's event will be supported by 50 Summa Health volunteers manning the aid stations along the course as well as over 100 Goodyear associates volunteering on race day. The final race in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health will be the 20th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, and Team Relay — following the Blue Line through the streets of Akron on Sept. 24, 2022. Additional 20th-year celebration activities include the Blue Jean Bash on Thurs., Sept. 22, 2022, at the John S. Knight Center. This will be the largest fundraising event for the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation and will feature food stations, an open bar, a live auction, live entertainment, running celebrities, a walk down the 20-year history of the Blue line, and much more! For ticket and sponsorship information please visit, akronmarathon.org/bluejeanbash. Race registration is still open, but limited spots remain for the Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k. To register or learn more about volunteer opportunities, simply visit akronmarathon.org

item.title: WINNERS ANNOUNCED IN THE GOODYEAR HALF MARATHON & 10K
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded: Akron, OH (Aug. 13, 2022) — More than 2,000 runners came together at Akron’s Goodyear Proving Grounds for the second race in the 8th annual Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. At the Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k, Nick Marino and Madeline Dawson were the winners in the men’s and women’s Goodyear Half Marathon, finishing at 1:10:02 and 1:17:32, respectively. Dawson’s time set a new women’s record for the event. The men’s 10k winner, Jacob Ondash, finished with a time of 30:53, setting a new event record for the men’s 10k. Ondash was also the winner of the National Interstate 1 Mile race in June, as part of the 2022 race series. The women’s 10k winner, Alyssa Thomas, finished with a time of 35:19. The Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k welcomed runners ages 12- 78 competing on Sat., Aug. 13, 2022, beginning at 6:30 a.m. “Hosting the Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k on our campus is a pride point for our company and the more than 200 Goodyear associates running or volunteering at the race,” said Doug Grassian, Senior Director for Global External and Digital Communications at The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company and Akron Marathon board director. “We congratulate all of the runners who participated and thank all of the volunteers and spectators for coming out to support the race.” “Congratulations to today’s race participants and event organizers for an outstanding event,” said Dr. Cliff Deveny, Summa Health’s President and CEO. “This year’s race series has served as another example of what makes our community great, and I look forward to the upcoming Akron Marathon in September.” The day’s winners included: HALF MARATHON FINAL RESULTS: MALE OVERALL 1. Nick Marino (Stow, OH) – 1:10:02 2. Will Appman (Hoboken, NJ) – 1:10:25 3. Zachary Hoagland (Hatfield, PA) – 1:10:30 FEMALE OVERALL 1. Madeline Dawson (Lakewood, OH) – 1:17:32 (new event record) 2. Catherine Joecken (Bay Village, OH) – 1:21:52 3. Amanda Fire (Stow, OH) 1:25:51 MASTER’S MALE 1. Paul Stock (Hudson, OH) – 1:21:32 2. Damon Blackford (Akron, OH) – 1:24:11 3. Volker Keim (Düsseldorf, NR, Germany) – 1:26:17 MASTER’S FEMALE 1. Rosanna Carlson (Akron, OH) – 1:36:13 2. Teresa Ferguson (Akron, OH) 1:39:10 3. Kellie Zajac (Akron, OH) – 1:39:55 10K FINAL RESULTS MALE OVERALL 1. Jacob Ondash (Cuyahoga Falls, OH) – 30:53 (new event record) 2. Luke Hickman (Mentor, OH) – 30:58 3. Martin Zegarelli (Kansas City, MO) – 32:51 FEMALE OVERALL 1. Alyssa Thomas (Cuyahoga Falls, OH) – 35:19 2. Becki Spellman (Galloway, OH) – 36:29 3. Andrea Klima (Independence, OH) – 37:57 MASTER’S MALE 1. Mark Rohrer (Wadsworth, OH) – 38:25 2. David Stewart (Mogadore, OH) – 38:29 3. Jason Brown (Homeworth, OH) – 40:13 MASTER’S FEMALE 1. Shelly Fountain (Minerva, OH) – 46:01 2. Maureen Foley (Cuyahoga Falls, OH) – 46:14 3. Maria Prinzo (Barberton, OH) – 46:22 The final race on Sept. 24, 2022, the marquee event and 20th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, and Team Relay — will follow the blue line through the streets of Downtown Akron. Race registration and volunteer opportunities for the final race series event can be found at AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: COUNTDOWN TO THE 20TH RUNNING OF THE AKRON MARATHON HAS BEGUN IN THE CITY OF AKRON
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
Akron, OH (Sept. 15, 2022) — Excitement and preparations are building for one of Akron’s largest sporting events of the year, the 20th running and marquee event of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay is set for Sat., Sept. 24, 2022. This year’s course, which will begin with a celebratory start, is a foot-tour through the city of Akron, highlighting the historic landmarks, colorful neighborhoods, and majestic Summit Metro Parks. Racers begin in downtown Akron and cross the All-America Bridge within the first mile. Runners will then weave through a course past the Akron Art Museum, The University of Akron, Firestone Park, the Towpath Trail, Sand Run Parkway, Stan Hywet estate, and Highland Square—where a world-class finish on Main Street at the Akron Civic Theatre and the popular Finisher Festival inside Lock 3 awaits them. The course description can be viewed here. The FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay will see more than 7,000 participants, 2,000 volunteers, and even more spectators. “With 20 years on the Blue Line, this race has grown to be a world-class running experience for our participants, which will be amplified this year thanks to a few surprises and nearly 100,000 spectators who will help us set that stage as a vital part of our race atmosphere in Akron,” states Anne Bitong, President & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “Whether you join us in support of one particular runner, or are there to cheer everyone on, we’re looking forward to seeing you along the Blue Line!” Here are ways to spectate in each of Akron’s five neighborhoods: Downtown Akron, Start Line, Miles 4, 5, 11, 12, and the Finish Line *The Finish Line will be live-streamed on the Akron Marathon’s Facebook page! First Runner: 7:00 a.m. Last Runner: 1:45 p.m.
  • Watch the start of the race north of the starting line on High Street between Market and MLK
  • Walk east one block using Market St towards Mile 3.7 (corner of Broadway St and Market St).
  • Walk south 3 blocks and turn left on University Ave. near Mile 11.3
  • Walk 2 blocks west to Main St. to see runners as they finish.
North Hill, Miles 1, 2, and 3 First Runner: 7:04 a.m. Last Runner: 8:10 a.m.
  • Cheer on the runners by lining N. Main St. to watch runners at Mile 1 and again at Mile 3 just north of the All-American Bridge.
Firestone Park, Miles 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 First Runner: 7:31 a.m. Last Runner: 9:55 a.m.
  • Cheer on the runners at Firestone Park at Mile 8.
Merriman Valley, Miles 16 and 17 First Runner: 8:24 a.m. Last Runner: 11:25 a.m.
  • Runners will be exiting the Ohio & Erie Canal Towpath Trail at Portage Path at Mile 16.7 on their approach to Mile 17 at Sand Run Metro Park.
West Akron, Miles 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, and 25 First Runner: 8:40 a.m. Last Runner: 1:25 p.m.
  • Cheer on the runners by lining the West Akron neighborhood during the runners’ most challenging miles.
Road closures will occur in each area during the active first-runner/last-runner times listed above. View Akron Marathon Road Closures for an extensive list and plan ahead! Or, looking to get more involved with the race? Volunteers are still needed: View available spots. For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health or volunteering, please visit AkronMarathon.org. # # # About the Akron Marathon Race Series The Akron Marathon Race Series is organized by the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, a nonprofit group founded in 2002 to provide a world-class marathon and other events that promote health and fitness, stimulate the local economy, galvanize the community and benefit charitable organizations. The series features race dates in June (National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile) and August (Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k), culminating with the 20th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, Team Relay & Kids Fun Run in September. Additional information is available at AkronMarathon.org or by calling (330) 434-2RUN (2786).

item.title: AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES PRESENTED BY SUMMA HEALTH ENDS WITH SUCCESSFUL 20TH RUNNING OF FIRSTENERGY AKRON MARATHON, HALF MARATHON, & TEAM RELAY AND CELEBRATES BLUE JEAN BASH
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
Akron, OH (Sept. 24, 2022) — Nearly 7,000 athletes and more than 100,000 spectators gathered at the marquee event of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, the 20th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay, which began with a celebratory start line at Akron Art Museum.  On a crisp and cool morning, the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay welcomed runners ages 12 to 80 competing from 38 different states and three countries on Sat., Sept. 24, 2022, beginning at 7:00 a.m.  Traveling 26.2 miles through the streets of Akron, the top finishers in today’s Marathon were  Zachary Hoagland from Hatfield, PA with a time of 2:25:58 and Alysia Rogers from Medina who finished with a time of 2:49:19. The first runners to cross the finish line outside of Lock 3 in the Half Marathon distance were Fernando Cabada of Aurora, CO and Alyssa Thomas from Cuyahoga Falls with times of 1:06:14 and 1:19:24.  Dylan Garritano from Akron was the runner-up in the men’s Marathon with a time of 2:28:41 while Ryan Hurley of Lakewood crossed the line third at 2:43:50. For the women, Emma McCarron of Westerville finished second with a time of 2:50:37 followed by Ro Morgan from Cortland in 2:56:37 in the Marathon. (Complete winner information can be found at the end of this release.) The Half Marathon had Nick Stricklen from Mansfield and Nathaniel Orndorf from Akron placing second and third in the men’s division. Becki Spellman from Galloway and Maura Lemon from Dayton rounded out the winner’s podium for the Women’s Half Marathon. Top times in the Master Division (40 years and older) were put up by Ryan Hurley and Barbara Lorson of Orrville in the Marathon. For the Half Marathon, the top Masters were Fernando Cabada (also the Half Marathon winner) and Michelle Bertenthal from Mayfield Heights. Prior to this marquee event, race week kicked off with the Blue Jean Bash on Thursday evening at the John S. Knight Center.  Friends and sponsors of the Akron Marathon gathered for the largest fundraiser to date for the Akron Marathon, hosted by Steve and Jeannine Marks, race co-founders, whose family also served as the presenting sponsor. Thanks to the generosity of donors from events like the Blue Jean Bash, the Akron Marathon can continue to improve health and wellness in Northeast Ohio. Throughout the Akron Marathon’s 20-year history, the organization has:
  • Celebrated 170,529 Blue Line Finishers
  • Raised over $6 million for charity
  • Generated $133 million of economic impact to the Greater Akron area
  • Provided 13,604 complimentary race entries
  • Accumulated over 132,740 volunteer hours
Friday night, the Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children’s Hospital had more than 500 youth ages 12 and under run their own “big race” along the one-mile course. Participating children ran and had the opportunity to cross the same finish line as the marquee event on Saturday.  “Congratulations to all runners who have demonstrated grit, discipline, and perseverance through their training and participation. We applaud your efforts and commend the time and talent you have dedicated to your sport,” said John Somerhalder, interim president and chief executive officer of FirstEnergy. “Special thanks are extended to all of those who have helped make this event a success, including race organizers, family, and friends who support our participants and the thousands of community members who turned out to volunteer and cheer runners along the way.” “Congratulations to all of the participants in this year’s Akron Marathon Race Series and to the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation for another outstanding year of races,” said Dr. Cliff Deveny, Summa Health president and CEO. “We’re proud to have been able to support this year’s events and look forward to next year and continuing our involvement in these important community events.” Plans are already underway for the 2023 Akron Marathon, and details will continue to be updated at AkronMarathon.org in the months to come. item.title: NONPROFIT AKRON MARATHON ANNOUNCES 2022 COMMUNITY IMPACT AND OPENING OF RACE REGISTRATION FOR 2023
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
Akron, OH (December 6, 2022) — It was a year of celebration for the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation as the nonprofit welcomed runners for the 20th running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay, as part of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. The Akron Marathon Race Series is organized by the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, a nonprofit founded in 2002 to promote health and fitness, stimulate the local economy, galvanize the community, and benefit charitable organizations through hosting its world-class marathon and other events. In 2022, the Akron Marathon hosted more than 10,000 runners across its 2022 events and 1,104 volunteers who gave 5,344 volunteer hours. Additionally, this event generated $6 million in economic impact for the Greater Akron area. Its updated Community Impact Report is now available. During the year, the Akron Marathon proudly:
  • Welcomed running celebrities at its 20th Health and Fitness Expo
  • Organized its largest fundraiser to date, the Blue Jean Bash, which was a tremendous success, and the funds raised will go directly to continuing health and wellness in our community
  • Held the 20th Kids Fun Run, which continues to be a free event thanks to the generous support of the City of Akron and Akron Children's Hospital
Part of the mission of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is to benefit nonprofit and charitable organizations. The Blue Line Charity Partner Program allows nonprofits from the community to use the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health as a fundraiser. During the 2022 racing season, charity partners raised $360,055 to benefit nonprofits in Greater Akron. The Akron Marathon also strives to promote healthy active lifestyles for all. Because of this, its team created the Runnership philanthropic program dedicated to reaching community members who could not typically afford a race entry, focusing on serving the underprivileged, disadvantaged, or those struggling with mental health and/or recovery. This year, 45 Runnership scholarships were given to runners in the community. “The pride we felt from being on the Blue Line with you and the way this community came together to celebrate the 20th running–it was an unforgettable year,” stated Anne Bitong, president & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. We’re honored to share numbers and data on how the running community truly supported each other. We can’t wait to be with you in 2023!” And now, the Marathon staff is gearing up for its 2023 Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health and is thrilled to announce dates and race registration has opened for 2023:
  • National Interstate 8K & 1 Mile, June 23 & 24, 2023
  • Goodyear Half Marathon & 10K, August 12, 2023
  • FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, and Team Relay: September 30, 2023
For more information, race registration, and volunteer opportunities for the final race series event, please visit AkronMarathon.org.

# # #

Contact:         Akron Marathon PR Contact Kat Allen, kat@ampstrategy.com 330-714-2274 Attached Photo Credit: Mike Cardew, Akron Beacon Journal About the Akron Marathon Race Series The Akron Marathon Race Series is organized by the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, a nonprofit group founded in 2002 to promote health and fitness, stimulate the local economy, galvanize the community, and benefit charitable organizations through hosting its world-class marathon and other events. The series features race dates in June (National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile) and August (Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k), culminating with the 21st running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, Team Relay & Kids Fun Run in September. Additional information is available at AkronMarathon.org or by calling (330) 434-2RUN (2786).

item.title: COUNTY OF SUMMIT INCREASES SUPPORT OF AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
[et_pb_section fb_built="1" admin_label="section" _builder_version="3.22"][et_pb_row admin_label="row" _builder_version="3.25" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat"][et_pb_column type="4_4" _builder_version="3.25" custom_padding="|||" custom_padding__hover="|||"][et_pb_text admin_label="Text" _builder_version="4.7.7" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat" hover_enabled="0" sticky_enabled="0"]

AKRON, Ohio (April 18, 2023) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is proud to announce a collaboration with the County of Summit for their Corporate Challenge and Blue Line Runnership programs.

The Corporate Challenge presented by the County of Summit is designed for local businesses to engage in friendly competition through participation in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. This turnkey solution enhances corporate wellness programs and allows companies to showcase their commitment to employee well-being and healthy workplace culture. Companies can apply by visiting akronmarathon.org/get-involved/corporate-challenge.

“We are excited to elevate our support of the Akron Marathon Race Series and invite businesses across Summit County to join us in incorporating the Akron Marathon Race Series as part of their comprehensive wellness programs,” states County Executive Ilene Shapiro. “We believe this collaboration is an ideal platform for corporate wellness, employee engagement, and a driver for healthier employees which is why we are thrilled to cover the cost of race entries for all county employees and hope that others follow suit.”

As a community nonprofit, the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation and its race series is dedicated to promoting health and wellness and creating events and programs that deliver opportunities to promote active lifestyles for all. Through its partnership with the county, 200 race entries will be distributed through its Blue Line Runnership Program. This philanthropic program is dedicated to reaching community members who could not typically afford a race entry, those wanting to strengthen their mental health, and/or add exercise to their addiction recovery plan. Applications are now open at akronmarathon.org/runnership.

"We are grateful for the generous support from the county and welcome businesses and individuals alike to join us for all three of our inspiring events,” states Anne Bitong, President & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “We take great pride in delivering memorable events that celebrate personal achievement and, with the county’s help, can remove barriers to registration so our events look representative of our community.”

Additionally, to prepare for the races, the Akron Marathon developed Training Plans and tips for participants. These comprehensive plans, tailored for walkers, beginning runners, and advanced athletes, provide weekly training plans and useful tips to help individuals cross the finish line of all three events.

The Akron Marathon Race Series will begin on June 23, 2023:

June 23, 2023: National Interstate Insurance 1 Mile

June 24, 2023: National Interstate Insurance 8K

August 12, 2023: Goodyear Half Marathon & 10K

September 29, 2023: Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children’s Hospital

September 30, 2023: FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, and Team Relay

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

item.title: AKRON MARATHON CHARITABLE CORPORATION ANNOUNCES NEW PRESENTING SPONSOR OF HEALTH AND FITNESS EXPO
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded: [et_pb_section fb_built="1" admin_label="section" _builder_version="3.22"][et_pb_row admin_label="row" _builder_version="3.25" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat"][et_pb_column type="4_4" _builder_version="3.25" custom_padding="|||" custom_padding__hover="|||"][et_pb_text admin_label="Text" _builder_version="3.27.4" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat"]Akron, OH (May 4, 2023) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is excited to announce the Akron Area YMCA as the new presenting sponsor for its annual Health and Fitness Expo. Both organizations share a commitment to promoting healthy and active lifestyles in the Northeast Ohio community and are dedicated to providing programs that empower individuals to live successful and healthy lives. Anne Bitong, President of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation shares, "As we continue to prioritize health and wellness at all levels in our community, we are thrilled to welcome the Akron Area YMCA as a new sponsor. Together, our nonprofits can continue to provide valuable resources and opportunities for individuals to lead healthier, more active lives." The Health and Fitness Expo, presented by the Akron Area YMCA, is a free event that is open to the public. This event kicks off the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay weekend. Attendees can look forward to race packet pick-up, official race merchandise, as well as exhibitors showcasing the latest health and fitness information and products. Organizations interested in participating as vendors at the Health and Fitness Expo can register now by visiting akronmarathon.org/race-series/akron-marathon/health-fitness-expo. This event provides an opportunity to showcase health and fitness products and services to over 10,000 attendees and to connect with members of the active Northeast Ohio community. “Bringing emphasis to the long-term vitality of the Akron area is so important,” said Jill Kolesar, President and CEO of the Akron Area YMCA. “Our involvement in this effort supports all that we do, every day, to assure that our community stays strong in spirit, mind, and body for many years to come.” The Akron Marathon Health and Fitness Expo will be held on Fri., Sept. 29, 2023, from 11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the John S. Knight Center. For more information about the event, visit akronmarathon.org/race-series/akron-marathon/health-fitness-expo.[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]
