The Health and Fitness Expo, presented by the Akron Area YMCA, is a free event that is open to the public. This event kicks off the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay weekend. Attendees can look forward to race packet pick-up, official race merchandise, as well as exhibitors showcasing the latest health and fitness information and products. Organizations interested in participating as vendors at the Health and Fitness Expo can register now by visiting akronmarathon.org/race-series/akron-marathon/health-fitness-expo. This event provides an opportunity to showcase health and fitness products and services to over 10,000 attendees and to connect with members of the active Northeast Ohio community. “Bringing emphasis to the long-term vitality of the Akron area is so important,” said Jill Kolesar, President and CEO of the Akron Area YMCA. “Our involvement in this effort supports all that we do, every day, to assure that our community stays strong in spirit, mind, and body for many years to come.” The Akron Marathon Health and Fitness Expo will be held on Fri., Sept. 29, 2023, from 11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the John S. Knight Center. For more information about the event, visit akronmarathon.org/race-series/akron-marathon/health-fitness-expo.

item.title: THE 2023 AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES PRESENTED BY SUMMA HEALTH SET TO KICK OFF JUNE 23
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, Ohio (June 14, 2023) — The Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health is excited to welcome runners embarking on their summer racing journeys, starting with the National Interstate Friday evening 1 Mile on June 23, 2023, at 7 p.m., followed by the 8k on Saturday, June 24, 2022, at 7:30 a.m. The Akron-based nonprofit Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation continues to foster inclusivity, encouraging individuals of all fitness levels to participate. In this three-event race series, with a diverse range of distances from 1 mile to a full marathon, participants are encouraged to select the race series distances that align with their personal goals. The National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile will feature a scenic course that winds through the heart of downtown Akron. Participants can expect a well-organized, professional event with support from dedicated volunteers. The National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile offers a unique opportunity for both seasoned runners and beginners to challenge themselves and achieve their fitness goals. “National Interstate is excited to kick off the Akron Marathon Race Series again in 2023!  We are honored to be a part of this alongside Goodyear, FirstEnergy, and Summa Health. Summit County and the City of Akron are filled with amazing organizations and people. We look forward to a great turnout for this series!” For optimal points and tips to view the runners in action, spectators can position themselves:
  • Watching runners begin on Spicer St., just outside InfoCision Stadium.
  • After the start, walk to Coleman Commons to the finish line on Carroll St., just beyond the Student Union.
  • For the 1 Mile, spectators wishing to see the finish may need to head to the finish line before the start of the race, as it is a half-mile away.
"Summa Health is dedicated to elevating the health of our community and we are proud to once again support the Akron Marathon Race Series," said Dr. Cliff Deveny, Summa Health president and CEO. "Together, with the Akron Marathon, we hope to inspire active lifestyles and build a stronger Akron, one step at a time. Good luck to everyone racing this season." Volunteer opportunities are still available for the June 23 and 24 events as well as the full race series. As a volunteer for the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, individuals and groups have the opportunity to make a significant contribution to the Greater Akron community, share skills/talents, and help make races successful world-class events for runners, their families, spectators, and the City of Akron. If you would like additional information on volunteering, please email Katie Riley, Community Outreach Director, or call the Marathon office at (330) 434-2786. Save the date for the much-anticipated Goodyear Half Marathon and 10k on Aug. 12, 2023. Additionally, mark your calendars for the marquee event, the 21st running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, and Team Relay, which will bring runners to the streets of Akron along the Blue Line on Sept. 30, 2023. For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, please visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: WEATHER ADVISORY ISSUED FOR THE AKRON MARATHON’S NATIONAL INTERSTATE 8K + 1 MILE
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
Akron, OH (June 23, 2023) — The Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health has sent a weather advisory and tips for running in the rain to its runners participating in the National Interstate 1 Mile on June 23, 2023, at 7 p.m. and its 8k on Saturday, June 24, 2022, at 7:30 a.m.

The National Weather Service is forecasting scattered showers with a chance of thunderstorms. Race officials have been and will continue to be in regular communication with the National Weather Service, and if the current forecast holds true, the temperature for the duration of the event will be mid-70s.

Saturday's race day forecast is calling for 62 degrees at the start increasing to 69 degrees at course closure. The National Weather Service is forecasting scattered showers with a low chance of thunderstorms beginning at 8:00 a.m. until 10:00 a.m.

“Providing a safe race for all is our top priority, but it is Ohio weather,” states Anne Bitong, president of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “We know our running community, and no matter the weather, they will bring their energy this weekend, show up for each other, and make it an unforgettable morning/evening of running. Should there be severe weather in the area, race organizers will delay the race in 15-minute increments for up to 1 hour.”

In the Akron Marathon race series history, its races have never been canceled due to weather.

Akron Marathon Medical Director, Dr. Shah, suggests, "If there are thunderstorms during the race, please follow the instructions of the Marathon staff to help you seek shelter," said Shah. “For the rain, the best thing to do is to just enjoy the refreshing rain, but make sure to use an anti-chafing balm.”

For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, please visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: THE 2023 AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES PRESENTED BY SUMMA HEALTH KICKS OFF WITH SOLD-OUT NATIONAL INTERSTATE 8K
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole

AKRON, OH (June 24, 2023) —  Dylan Garritano from Akron secured the 8k victory in the men's division of the National Interstate 8k for the second consecutive year, while Meghann Featherstun from Kent triumphed in the women's division. This event marked the beginning of the 2023 Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, taking place on Fri., evening June 23, 2023, and Sat., June 24, 2023. The sold-out National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile attracted over 1,800 participants from 10 states and 3 countries, spanning ages from 0 (thanks to the popular stroller division of the 1 Mile) to 78. The course for the National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile began by highlighting The University of Akron's campus, offering a unique tour of downtown Akron. As with all courses in this series, the course caters to individuals of various fitness levels, accommodating both runners and walkers as they strive towards the finish lines. “It’s an honor to extend a warm welcome to our athletes who kickstarted the racing season for us this morning,” states Anne Bitong President and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “Our nonprofit felt the energy in the streets of Akron this weekend, and we’re so grateful to all levels of supporters! From the runners to the sponsors and volunteers, strong partners are the foundation of the success of our world-class race series.” The first runners to cross the finish line Friday in the 1 Mile race were Ryan Kiley from Cuyahoga Falls and Kelly Valco from Akron. National Interstate Insurance, in its eighth year as presenting sponsor, cheered as Kiley–one of its 60 employees participating–took home the win. “National Interstate is excited to have kicked off the Akron Marathon Race Series again in 2023," states Tony Prinzo, VP of Human Resources at National Interstate. item.title: KEIRA D’AMATO NAMED 2023 AKRON MARATHON AMBASSADOR
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, Ohio (June 28, 2023) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is delighted to announce Keira D'Amato as the official Ambassador for the 2023 Akron Marathon. D'Amato, who recently announced her participation as a member of USA Track & Field's Team USA at the World Championships Marathon in Budapest, Hungary this summer, will be cheered on by the northeast Ohio running community before she visits Akron later this fall. Recipients of the Akron Marathon Ambassador Award have made significant contributions and lasting impacts on the sport of running.

D'Amato has emerged as a remarkable long-distance runner and a rising star in the running world. Her exceptional achievements, such as her qualification for the 2021 Olympic Trials and her record-breaking performance as the American marathon record holder with a time of 2:19:12 at the 2022 Houston Marathon, have solidified her position as a force to be reckoned with in the running community. D'Amato's passion for the sport, combined with her unwavering commitment to excellence, makes her an ideal choice as the Akron Marathon Ambassador.

"We are pleased to announce Keira D'Amato as our Ambassador for the 2023 Akron Marathon," said Anne Bitong, President & CEO of the Akron Marathon. "Her achievements as a runner are truly remarkable, and we are excited to support her journey at the Marathon World Championships in Budapest. We look forward to welcoming her race weekend."

During her visit to Akron, which will take place from Sept. 27 to Sept. 29, 2023, D'Amato will participate in events including the VIP party on Wed., Sept. 27, where she will be honored with the 13th annual Akron Marathon Ambassador Award as well as the Health & Fitness Expo on Fri. Sept. 29 where registered participants will have the opportunity to meet D’Amato and gain insights from her training experiences and receive encouragement for their own journeys.

“I am totally honored to be named the Ambassador for the 2023 Akron Marathon," said Keira D'Amato. "As I prepare to represent Team USA at the World Championships Marathon, it is incredibly special to receive the support of the Akron community. I look forward to connecting with participants at the Health & Fitness Expo, giving out as many high fives as possible, and sharing my joy for running. See you soon, Akron!!”

To learn more about D'Amato and her remarkable journey, please visit her official website at keiradamato.com, or for more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, please visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES PRESENTED BY SUMMA HEALTH CONTIUNES ON AUG.12 WITH NEARLY SOLD-OUT GOODYEAR HALF MARATHON AND 10K
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
Akron, OH (Aug. 3, 2023) – The Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health is hosting the second event of its series, the nearly sold-out Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k, taking place on Aug. 12, 2023.

The Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k was designed for runners and walkers alike, who will begin the course with a lap around the Goodyear Test Track at the Akron Proving Grounds. The route will then lead participants through Akron's East End and Ellet neighborhoods, with a memorable finish under the skywalk of Goodyear's Global Headquarters.

“Hosting the Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k is extra special for us this year as we celebrate our 125-year legacy in Akron,” said Doug Grassian, senior director, global external and digital communications, and Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation Board Director. “It’s always gratifying to see the presence of the community at this race including the more than 200 Goodyear associates running and volunteering."

The Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k, the second race in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, promises an unforgettable experience, featuring the ever-popular Finisher Festival that has become a hallmark of the Akron Marathon Race Series. Participants look forward to a variety of vendors and displays, including the highly anticipated presence of Swenson's Food Trucks, OH Donut Co., Sandy Bottom Bowls, and the Roll by Goodyear vehicle.

Each participant will receive a premium short sleeve performance shirt and a commemorative medal which will feature the historic Goodyear Wingfoot logo, originally created in 1898, to celebrate Goodyear's 125th anniversary year.

Packet Pick-Up for this race is scheduled for Fri., Aug. 11, 2023, from 11:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. at the John S. Knight Center. Runners have been asked to collect their race packets during this designated time, as race day packet pick-up will not be available.

The final race in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health will be the 21st running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay — following the Blue Line through the streets of Akron on Sept. 30, 2023.

Limited spots remain for the Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k, with online race registration open through Aug. 7, 2023. To secure your spot or explore volunteer opportunities, please visit akronmarathon.org.

item.title: COUNTDOWN TO THE 21ST RUNNING OF THE AKRON MARATHON HAS BEGUN IN THE CITY OF AKRON
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
Akron, OH (Sept. 5, 2023) — Excitement is building for the 21st running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay, the marquee event of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. Akron’s largest single-day sporting event of the year is set for Sat., Sept. 30, 2023.

The course features a foot-tour through the city of Akron, highlighting the historic landmarks, colorful neighborhoods, and majestic Summit Metro Parks. Thousands are scheduled to begin in downtown Akron and cross the All-America Bridge within the first mile.

Runners will journey through the heart of the city, passing by cultural gems like the Akron Art Museum, The University of Akron, Firestone Park, the Towpath Trail, Sand Run Parkway, Stan Hywet estate, and Highland Square. The ultimate finish line awaits on S. Main Street in front of Canal Park, for an extraordinary conclusion to this world-class race, followed by the popular Finisher Festival filled with food trucks and music by local cover band Roxxymoron.

Energizing the festivities the day before the race is The Akron Marathon Health & Fitness Expo presented by the Akron Area YMCA, from 11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Open to the public at no charge, the expo not only offers race packet pick-up, but also showcases exhibitors’ presenting the latest in health and fitness insights and products as well as the Akron Marathon Official Merchandise Store.

The Expo's Main Stage will host an array of guests, like Keira D'Amato, giving insights from her marathon training exploits, while also encouraging runners on their personal journeys. Sharing the spotlight is Martinus Evans, author of Slow AF Run Club, podcast host, and featured New York Times and Runner’s World athlete, on a mission to inspire with his message of "300 pounds and running." Limited vendor spots remain available—interested parties can visit the vendor registration on the Marathon’s website to secure their place.

As the sun sets on the eve of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay, the Marathon will host hundreds of young walkers and runners in the Kids Fun Run—an event designed exclusively for children aged 12 and under. The memorable event is free of charge and a gift to the community by Akron Children’s Hospital and the City of Akron.

"As we eagerly await to kick off the 21st running of the Akron Marathon, we’re honored by our community and their commitment to their health journeys and our nonprofit,” states Anne Bitong, President/CEO. “Marathon weekend stands as a true testament to the unity and resilience of our community, a culmination of months, maybe years, of preparation and dedication. It's more than a race on the Blue Line in Akron; it's a celebration of your potential, camaraderie, and the unwavering spirit that defines our city.”

Schedule of Events:

●      Fri., Sept. 29, 2023: The Akron Marathon Health & Fitness Expo presented by the Akron Area YMCA, from 11:00 AM to 8:00 PM: Blue Line Main Stage Schedule, Vendor List

●      Fri., Sept. 29, 2023: Kids Fun Run: Start at 5:30 PM: 214 W. Bowery St., At Akron Children’s Hospital: Course Map

●      Sat., Sept. 30, 2023: The FirstEnergy Full Marathon, Half Marathon, and Team Relay: Start at 7:00 AM with Wheelchair & Push Teams at 6:59 AM.: Akron Art Museum 1 S. High St, Akron: Parking Information, Course Description, Course Maps (scroll to middle of the page to view), and Day of Road Closures 

The FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay will see more than 8,000 participants, 2,000 volunteers, and even more spectators. Online registration will close on Sun., Sept. 24.

 

Here are ways to spectate in each of Akron’s five neighborhoods:

 

Downtown Akron, Start Line, Miles 3.7,11, and the Finish Line 

First Runner: 7:00 a.m.

Last Runner: 8:10 a.m.

Watch the start of the race north of the starting line on High Street between Market and MLK

Walk east one block using Market St towards Mile 3.7 (corner of Broadway St and Market St). Walk south 3 blocks and turn left on University Ave. to see racers near Mile 11 and finally, walk 2 blocks west to S. Main St. to see participants as they approach the finish.

North Hill, Miles 1, 2, and 3

First Runner: 7:05 a.m.

Last Runner: 7:55 a.m.

Cheer on the runners by lining N. Main St. to watch runners at Mile 1 and again at Mile 3 just north of the All-American Bridge.

Firestone Park, Miles 7 and 8

First Runner: 7:36 a.m.

Last Runner: 9:10 a.m.

Cheer on the runners at Firestone Park at Mile 8.

Merriman Valley, Miles 16 and 17

First Runner: 8:22 a.m.

Last Runner: 11:25 a.m.

Runners will be exiting the Ohio & Erie Canal Towpath Trail at Portage Path at Mile 16.2 on their approach to Mile 17 at Sand Run Metro Park.

West Akron, Miles 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, and 25

First Runner: 8:38 a.m.

Last Runner: 1:25 p.m.

Cheer on the runners by lining the West Akron neighborhood during the runners’ most challenging miles.

Road closures will occur in each area during the active first-runner/last-runner times listed above which can also be found on the Akron Marathon Course Map. View Akron Marathon Road Closures for an extensive list and plan ahead!

The Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health is organized by the nonprofit Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation whose mission is to promote health and wellness in the community. For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health or the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: AKRON’S DYLAN GARRITANO WINS AKRON MARATHON, SWEEPING THE SERIES
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded: Akron, OH (Sept. 30, 2023) — More than 7,000 athletes and nearly 100,000 spectators gathered for the marquee event of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay on Sat., Sept. 30, 2023, beginning at 7:00 a.m. Traveling 26.2 miles through the blue-lined streets of Akron at 2:25:06 and 2:52:03; Dylan Garritano of Akron and Joanna Line of Hiram were the top finishers in today’s marathon. City of Akron employee Garritano is a “three-peat” winner– taking the win on all three of the Akron Marathon Race Series Presented by Summa Health events including today’s Full Marathon, the Goodyear Half Marathon, and the National Interstate 8k. This morning’s cool and crisp weather was described as “the perfect running weather” by athletes of all fitness levels who participated from 37 states, three countries, with ages ranging from four years old (on a push team) to 82 years old. The first runners to cross the finish line in the half marathon distance were Chad Johnson of Galion and Hannah Moulton of Ann Arbor, MI with times of 1:07:10 and 1:17:55. Ethan Cannon of Minneapolis, MN was the runner-up in the men’s marathon with a time of 2:28:02, while Charles Smogoleski of Eaton Rapids, MI crossed the line third at 2:29:12. For the women’s division of the marathon, Christina Johnston of Xenia finished second with a time of 2:54:36 followed by Ashley Letteney from Rochester, NY in 3:01:15. (Complete winner information can be found at the end of this release.) The half marathon had Collin Oswalt from Hutchinson, KS, and Luke Hickman from Mentor, placing second and third in the men’s division. Andrea Klima from Independence and Jennifer Simmerman from Streetsboro rounded out the winner’s podium for the women’s half marathon. Top times in the Master’s Division (40 years and older) were put up by John Ladesic of Olney, MD, and Christina Johnston of Xenia in the marathon. For the half marathon, the top masters were Matthias Wilder of Winter Garden, FL, and Jennifer Simmerman of Streetsboro. Simmerman set a new event record in the women’s Master’s Division with a time of 1:23:59. “The Akron community has once again united in support of the Blue Line,” shared Anne Bitong, president/CEO of the Akron Marathon. “With remarkable race times, the dedication of thousands of volunteers, and the unwavering support of our generous sponsors, we are thrilled with how Akron showed up today!” Along the Blue Line, stories inspired those participating, like that of Josh Sommers who competed in his 7th Akron Marathon—but today marked the first time he participated in the Male Wheelchair division. In 2022, Sommers was in a motorcycle accident that paralyzed him from the chest down. Josh shared with the Marathon team, “I was not able to participate in last year's Marathon due to the accident, but I was able to start learning how to race in a wheelchair last November. It gives me a sense of accomplishment, but more than that, when I cross the finish line, I prove to myself that if I can finish a marathon, I am strong enough to persevere when life throws me curve balls…In those hard times, I can look back to finishing the race and find the strength to keep going. I am celebrating the fact that I can still participate in the Akron Marathon even though it may not be in the traditional way.” Plans are already underway for the 2024 Akron Marathon, which marks the 10th year of the Akron Marathon Race Series. Details will continue to be updated at AkronMarathon.org in the months to come. FULL MARATHON Male 1. Dylan Garritano, Akron, 2:25:06 2. Ethan Cannon, Minneapolis, MN, 2:28:02 3. item.title: AKRON MARATHON CHARITABLE CORPORATION CELEBRATES SUCCESS OF CORPORATE CHALLENGE PROGRAM
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded: Akron, OH (Nov. 28, 2023) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is honored to announce the success of its Corporate Challenge Program, sponsored by the County of Summit. The Corporate Challenge has proven to be a catalyst for a fun and competitive environment, promoting health, fitness, and wellness at every level in the local business community. From couch to 8k, to first-time marathoners, this challenge provides a turnkey program that seamlessly integrates into corporate wellness initiatives. “Summit County businesses have always been collaborative partners and we knew the Corporate Challenge would be another great way for businesses large and small to get involved,” said Summit County Executive Ilene Shapiro. “The initiative not only promotes health and wellness but helps strengthen that sense of community that makes Summit County such a special place to work and live.” More than 1,200 runners across 34 companies participated in the Corporate Challenge this racing season, turning it into a platform for a healthy and vibrant corporate culture. The awards ceremony took place on Nov. 21, 2023, at the Summit County Chambers, and honored outstanding achievements and celebrated the winners in various categories. Participation Division Winners: Scheeser Buckley Mayfield - 23 runners Slater & Zurz Law Firm - 10 runners Cascade Auto Group - 5 runners The J.M. Smucker Company - 34 runners National Interstate Insurance - 102 runners The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co. - 265 runners Fastest Corporate Challenge Relay Team Award: Charles Schwab - Fastest Men’s Relay Team FocusCFO - Fastest Women’s Relay Team GPD Group - Fastest Mixed Relay Team Company with the Most Volunteers: Summa Health - 95 volunteers “We’re thrilled to see the tremendous success of the Corporate Challenge Program,” states Anne Bitong, President/CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “The strong participation from local businesses is a testament to this incredible race series; it's a celebration of wellness, teamwork, and community spirit.” Looking to participate in 2024? Registration for the Akron Marathon Race Series officially opens on Jan. 10, 2024. To check eligibility for discounted race entry fees, contact your Employee Wellness Coordinator. For questions or additional information, please contact Katie Riley at 330-434-2786 or via email at kriley@akronmarathon.org. The Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health is organized by the nonprofit Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation whose mission is to promote health and wellness in the community. For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health or the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: 10-YEAR CELEBRATION OF THE AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES SET FOR JUNE 28 & 29
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, O.H. (June 19, 2024) — The Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health is thrilled to kick off the 10-year celebration, welcoming participants to the National Interstate 1 Mile Friday evening on June 28, 2024, at 7:00 p.m., and the 8k on Saturday, June 29, 2024, at 7:30 a.m. The Akron-based nonprofit, Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, remains committed to fostering inclusivity and welcoming all individuals to join in the celebration and participate in the festivities. “As we kick off the 10th year of the Akron Marathon Race Series, were excited to celebrate a decade dedicated to promoting community wellness,” states Anne Bitong, president, and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “This milestone reflects our ongoing mission to inspire health and fitness across the greater Akron area and beyond. We are grateful for the unwavering support of our participants and community." The Akron Marathon Race Series promotes health, fitness, and community spirit, encouraging individuals to pursue personal achievements through participation in its diverse range of distances, spanning from 1 mile to a full marathon. "Summa Health is committed to enhancing the well-being of our community, and we are delighted to continue our support for the Akron Marathon Race Series," states Dr. Cliff Deveny, president, and CEO of Summa Health. "In collaboration with the Akron Marathon, we aim to encourage active lifestyles and contribute to the resilience of Akron, step by step. Best wishes to all participants in this season's races." The National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile will feature a scenic course that starts at The University of Akron and winds through the heart of downtown Akron before returning to campus. With 11 returning champions, excitement is building for a thrilling race. This event provides a unique opportunity for seasoned athletes, beginners, and families to come together for a fun-filled celebration of fitness. “National Interstate is extremely proud to have kicked off the tenth running of the Akron Marathon Race Series with the 8k & 1-mile event,” states Tony Prinzo, VP of human resources at National Interstate. “Health and wellness are key tenants of our award winning, employee-driven culture, and we are thrilled to support the Race Series to not only benefit our team members, but also the community of greater Akron and Summit County.” For optimal viewing points spectators can position themselves:
  • Watch the race start on Spicer St., just outside InfoCision Stadium
  • After the start, walk through Coleman Common to the finish line on Carroll St., just beyond the Student Union
  • For the 1 Mile, spectators wishing to see the finish may need to head to the finish line before the start of the race, as it is a half-mile away.
Save the date for the highly anticipated Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k on August 10, 2024, and mark your calendars for the flagship event, the 22nd edition of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay, along the Blue Line on September 28, 2024.

item.title: 10-YEAR CELEBRATION OF THE AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES CONTINUES WITH THE GOODYEAR HALF MARATHON & 10K
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, O.H. (July 31, 2024) – The Akron Marathon Race Series, presented by Summa Health, gears up for the second event of its series—the highly anticipated 10th annual Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k! This event is set to take place on Aug. 10, 2024, at 6:30 a.m., and will bring nearly 2,500 participants from all over to enjoy a fantastic day of racing. The Akron Marathon Race Series, organized by the nonprofit Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, promotes health, fitness, and community spirit. Designed to complement a typical marathon training program, the series offers three distinct race experiences. Among them, the Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k stands out as one of the most popular events, celebrated for its iconic Akron setting with Goodyear serving as the venue host. "We are thrilled to celebrate the 10th year of the Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k," said Anne Bitong, president & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. "This race is a hallmark Akron experience, highlighting our community’s commitment to health, wellness, and unity. With continued support of Goodyear and Summa Health, we’re proud to promote an active lifestyle for all." Adding to the celebration, The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company is proudly extending its presenting sponsorship. “Goodyear is proud to extend our partnership with the Akron Marathon Race Series through 2027," said Doug Grassian, vice president, global communications of The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company and Akron Marathon board member. “Our commitment to this event underscores our dedication to fostering a strong, healthy, and connected community.” The Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k kicks off with a lap around the historic Goodyear Test Track at the Akron Proving Grounds, weaving through Akron's East End and Ellet neighborhoods, culminating with a triumphant finish at Goodyear's Global Headquarters. For optimal viewing, spectators can choose from the following options:
  • Inside the test track for the start and at mile 1.
  • Outside the test track, viewing participants at mile 1, then at mile 4.1, moving 0.3 miles north to the finish line.
  • Finish Line for mile 1.3, walking 0.2 miles south to the traffic circle for mile 4, then returning to the finish line
The Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k promises an unparalleled experience, featuring the celebrated Finisher Festival—a staple of this event. Participants can look forward to live music and a variety of food trucks, including the irresistible flavors of Swenson's Food Trucks, Sandy Bottom Bowls, and the American Chuck Wagon. Showcased at the finish line are branded vehicles featuring Goodyear's One Lap of America car, which impressively took first place in the 40th running of One Lap of America this year. Participants can capture photos with these vehicles and explore the Goodyear merchandise. The culminating event in the series will be the 22nd annual FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay, taking place on September 28, 2024. For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, please visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: WINNERS ANNOUNCED IN THE 10TH ANNUAL GOODYEAR HALF MARATHON & 10K

AKRON, OH (Aug. 10, 2024) — Nearly 2,300 athletes came together at Goodyear’s Akron Proving Grounds Test Track for the second event in the 10th annual Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health on Sat., Aug. 10, 2024, beginning at 6:30 a.m.

The Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k welcomed participants from ages 5 to 81, from 29 states and 4 countries. The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company proudly announced the extension of its presenting sponsorship through 2027, in celebration of the 10th year.

Israel Merkle and Andrea Klima were the Goodyear Half Marathon men’s and women’s division winners, finishing at 1:12:04 and 1:21:07. The men’s 10k winner, Luke Hickman, finished with a time of 31:51, and the women’s 10k winner, Ashton Swinford, finished with a time of 36:40.

item.title: The Mandel Family Donates Major Gift to Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation’s Kids Fun Run
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded: AKRON, O.H. (Aug. 13, 2024) – The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is proud to announce a transformative donation from philanthropists Thom and Lisa Mandel to support its annual Kids Fun Run. In recognition of their generous support, the event will now be named "The Mandel Family Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children's Hospital."  Thom and Lisa Mandel's contribution represents a significant commitment to promoting children's health and wellness in our community. Their generous donation will support the ongoing success and growth of the Kids Fun Run, ensuring the event remains free as an integral part of the Akron Marathon weekend festivities.   "We are thrilled to support the Akron Marathon Kids Fun Run alongside Akron Children's Hospital," said Thom and Lisa Mandel. "Encouraging children to lead active lifestyles aligns closely with our values, and we are honored to be part of an event that brings joy and promotes healthy habits among young participants."   The renaming of the Kids Fun Run to honor the Mandel's underscores their dedication to making a positive impact on the lives of children in Akron. Their commitment not only supports the event's mission but also emphasizes the importance of community engagement and philanthropy.   "We are incredibly grateful to Thom and Lisa Mandel for their extraordinary generosity," said Jeannine Marks, founder of Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. "Their gift will enhance our ability to provide a memorable and impactful experience for our youngest participants, inspiring them to embrace active lifestyles and strive for their personal best."     The event will include a 1 Mile fun run, a range of activities tailored for children, and vendors that encourage physical activity and healthy habits, all within a festive and supportive atmosphere. The Mandel's gift will be officially celebrated during Akron’s marathon weekend on September 27 and 28.    For more information about The Mandel Family Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children's Hospital, please visit AkronMarathon.org/KidsFunRun.

item.title: AKRON MARATHON CHARITABLE CORPORATION ANNOUNCES BRET TREIER AS 2024 AMBASSADOR AWARD RECIPIENT
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, O.H. (Aug. 27, 2024) – The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is proud to announce that Bret Treier, a long-time volunteer, original course designer, and Board Emeritus, has been named the 2024 Ambassador Award Recipient. Treier will be honored at the Akron Marathon’s annual VIP Party on Wednesday, Sept. 25, 2024, at House Three Thirty. 

Bret Treier has been an integral part of the Akron Marathon since its inception. As one of the original course designers, his vision helped shape the event into the celebrated race it is today. Over the years, Treier has devoted countless hours to volunteering and contributing to the growth and success of the event, serving as course co-chair, board member, and chair. Under his guidance, the event has grown from 3,000 to 12,000 participants across three events, yielding an economic impact of $6 million annually. Treier has witnessed over 188,000 blue liners cross the finish line. His dedication and passion for the Akron Marathon have made a lasting impact on the community and the organization itself.

In addition to his contributions to the Akron Marathon, Bret is a seasoned runner in his own right. He has completed more than 60 marathons and ultra marathons, including 12 Boston Marathons. Included in that number are many blue line practice runs with race organizers over the years to check course conditions in real time. He has also competed in dozens of distance relays including Hood to Coast, the Bourbon Chase, and our local Burning River. Before getting involved in our Akron Marathon, Bret helped organize many local races and community events, including the Canal Park 5k, the YMCA Triathlon, and the YMCA Jack-O-Lantern Jog. He also is proud to have organized the very first Relay for Life in Ohio for the American Cancer Society. This list is not comprehensive but stands to showcase his personal commitment to the sport and the running community.

“We are thrilled to honor Bret Treier with the 2024 Ambassador Award,” said Steve and Jeannine Marks, race founders. “His contributions to the Akron Marathon and his unwavering commitment to our mission have been invaluable. Bret's dedication to the running community exemplifies the spirit of the Akron Marathon.”  

The Ambassador Award is presented annually to an individual who has made significant contributions and lasting impact on the sport of running. This award honors those who inspire others to run through their commitment and enthusiasm. This year, Treier will be honored as the 2024 Ambassador Award Recipient during the race weekend.

The Akron Marathon, now in its 22nd year, continues to be a premier event that attracts participants from across the nation. The race weekend includes the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, Team Relay, and The Mandel Family Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children’s Hospital, providing opportunities for runners of all ages and abilities to participate.

item.title: 22ND ANNUAL FIRSTENERGY AKRON MARATHON, HALF MARATHON & TEAM RELAY SET FOR SEPT. 27-28, 2024
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, O.H. (Aug. 29, 2024) – The FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay is excited to welcome participants to its 22nd annual event on Sept. 27-28, 2024. This year promises to be unforgettable, with new features and cherished traditions designed to celebrate every finisher’s achievements. Marathon weekend is one of Akron’s beloved traditions, and race organizers invite the entire community to run, walk, cheer, or volunteer. Community-wide participation helps create the vibrant and supportive atmosphere that makes this event special year after year. Health & Fitness Expo presented by the Akron Area YMCA Kicks Off Race Weekend The festivities begin on Friday, Sept. 27, with the Health and Fitness Expo presented by the Akron Area YMCA at the John S. Knight Center, located at 77 E. Mill St, Akron. The Expo, open from 11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., is free and open to the public. It features race packet pickup, where participants can collect their race bib, shirt, and other essential items before the big day. Additionally, the Expo offers official race merchandise and dozens of exhibitors. Attendees can enjoy motivational speakers on the Blue Line Main Stage like Ali Feller, the renowned host of the popular "Ali on the Run Show" podcast and unwind in the Runners Lounge with KT taping and Normatec boots. The Mandel Family Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children’s Hospital Promises Family Fun Also on Friday, families are invited to The Mandel Family Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children's Hospital. This free event starts at 214 W. Bowery St and finishes at 300 S. Main St, near Canal Park. The registration tent opens at 5:00 p.m., and the race starts at 6:00 p.m. With over 1,000 kids expected to participate, it’s a joyful event where children can run, walk, hop, skip, and jump to the finish line. We are delighted to welcome the Mandel Family as new supporters and thank them for their generous support. Main Event: FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay The main event takes place on Saturday, Sept. 28, starting with the Opening Ceremony at 6:00 a.m. The FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay begins at 7:00 a.m. at the Akron Art Museum, 1 S. High St, Akron, and finishes on S. Main St outside Canal Park. Participants will traverse a scenic route through Akron's neighborhoods and historic landmarks, with entertainment and block parties at every mile. After crossing the finish line, participants can celebrate at the FirstEnergy Finisher Festival, featuring live music, food trucks, and more. Join the Excitement:  Volunteer for Race Weekend We're looking for enthusiastic volunteers to help make race weekend unforgettable! From supporting runners and managing fluid stations to cheering on participants, there are many ways to get involved. Volunteers receive a free event t-shirt, a commemorative pin, and the chance to be part of Akron's cherished tradition. Sign up at https://www.akronmarathon.org/volunteer/ to join the fun and make a difference! Schedule of Events Friday, Sept. 27
  • Health & Fitness Expo presented by the Akron Area YMCA:
John S. Knight Center, 77 E. Mill St, Akron 11:00 a.m. - Doors Open 8:00 p.m. - Doors Close
  • The Mandel Family Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children’s Hospital:
Start at 214 W. Bowery St, Finish at 300 S. Main St 5:00 p.m. - Registration Tent / Bib Pick-Up Opens 6:00 p.m. - Race Start 6:45 p.m. - Course Closes 7:30 p.m. - Venue Closes Saturday, Sept. 28
  • FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay:
Start at Akron Art Museum, 1 S. High St, Akron, Finish at Downtown Akron 6:00 a.m. – Opening Ceremony 6:59 a.m. – Wheelchair Division & Push Team Start 7:00 a.m. - Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay Start 7:35 a.m. – FirstEnergy Finisher Festival Opens 8:50 a.m. – Half Marathon Overall Awards 10:45 a.m. Marathon Overall Awards 1:40 p.m. – Course Closes 1:45 p.m. – Finisher Festival Closes "We are incredibly grateful to Summa Health for being the presenting series sponsor and to FirstEnergy for their longstanding support as the presenting sponsor of marathon weekend. Their unwavering commitment plays a crucial role in making this event a success year after year,” said Anne Bitong, president & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “A heartfelt thank you to the City of Akron, the Akron Police & Fire Departments, our amazing volunteers, and all our generous sponsors. Your support is what makes this event possible." For more information and to register to run, walk, cheer, or volunteer, visit www.akronmarathon.org or follow us on social media @AkronMarathon.

item.title: FIRSTENERGY RENEWS COMMITMENT AS PRESENTING SPONSOR OF THE AKRON MARATHON, HALF MARATHON & TEAM RELAY THROUGH 2027
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, O.H. (Sept. 26, 2024) – The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is proud to announce the renewal of its partnership with FirstEnergy Corp. as the presenting sponsor of the Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay through 2027. This continued collaboration further strengthens a bond that has been in place since the race’s inception, demonstrating FirstEnergy's steadfast commitment to the Akron community and the race that brings it together.

Since the beginning, FirstEnergy has played a vital role in the success of the Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay, with more than 100 of their employees lacing up each year to run in the event. Their support goes beyond financial contributions, as they continually provide volunteers and resources, embodying the "Experience the Energy" branding that will appear on sponsorship elements throughout the event including an enhanced FirstEnergy Finisher Festival and block party kits. In alignment with FirstEnergy's commitment to sustainability, the sponsorship renewal will support new green initiatives for the 2025 races, including HydraPak cups that reduce the use of paper cups at fluid stations as well as branded shoe recycling stations.

"We are proud to continue our partnership with the Akron Marathon," said Brian X. Tierney, president and CEO of FirstEnergy Corp. “Stewardship is a core value at FirstEnergy that we embrace through our involvement in our local communities, including marquee events like the Marathon. It’s more than just a race; it's a celebration of community, resilience, and the energy that drives us all forward. We’re also pleased to add sustainability elements to our sponsorship that will support a healthy environment."

"We are grateful to FirstEnergy for their unwavering support over the years," said Anne Bitong, president & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corp. "Their dedication to the Akron Marathon has been a cornerstone of our success, and we are thrilled to continue this journey with them. Together, we will not only deliver an exceptional race experience but also pioneer sustainable practices that will benefit our community for years to come."

item.title: WINNERS ANNOUNCED IN THE 22ND ANNUAL FIRSTENERGY AKRON MARATHON, HALF MARATHON & TEAM RELAY
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, O.H. (Sept. 28, 2024) — Akron was lively today as nearly 8,000 athletes and 100,000 spectators gathered for the marquee event of the 2024 Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. The FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay brought together athletes from across the nation and beyond, highlighting the city’s commitment to health and community. Headlining the sold-out marathon was Aaron Davidson from Flagstaff, AZ, with a time of 2:25:30. Davidson successfully chased redemption, securing victory after his withdrawal from the 2024 Olympic Trials. In the women’s division, Maura Lemon of Dayton claimed victory, crossing the finish line with an impressive time of 2:52:37. A former champion, Lemon had previously won the 2016 FirstEnergy Half Marathon with a time of 1:18:25. The FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay welcomed athletes from ages 12 to 80. Participants came from 41 U.S. states and 6 countries, adding to the marathon’s reputation as one of the premier running events in the Midwest. In the half marathon, Alec Sandusky of Cincinnati took the men’s title with a blazing time of 1:07:30, while Alyssa Thomas of Cuyahoga Falls led the women’s division with a strong finish of 1:18:35, beating her winning time from 2022. In the newly introduced non-binary category, Grace Barnard from Stow claimed first place in the marathon, and Emily Donley from Broadview Heights excelled in the half marathon, reflecting our ongoing commitment to inclusivity. The city came alive as runners wound their way through 13 of Akron’s most iconic neighborhoods, with supporters lining the Blue Line to cheer on athletes. From Firestone Park to the West Akron, the route showcased Akron’s vibrant community spirit. "We’re thrilled with the success of this year's Akron Marathon Race Series, said Anne Bitong, president & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “The energy from the community, the dedication of the participants, and the support from our sponsors–FirstEnergy,  Summa Health, and the City of Akron–are what make this event so special. Our mission has always been to promote health, fitness, and community spirit, and it's inspiring to see how the marathon continues to bring people together in pursuit of these goals." This year’s Akron Marathon Race Series Corporate Challenge, presented by the County of Summit, saw an incredible turnout with 1,349 participants from 33 organizations. Final standings for the Corporate Challenge will be announced later this fall. The weekend festivities kicked off with Friday’s Mandel Family Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children’s Hospital. Nearly 1,000 young runners, ages 12 and under, had their moment to shine as they raced the one-mile course to cross the same finish line as the marathoners, greeted by cheering crowds and family members. Planning is already underway for the 2025 edition of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, which once again aims to rally the community around health, wellness, and fun. Mark your calendars for the National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile on June 27 & 28, the Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k on August 9, and the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay on September 27. item.title: AKRON MARATHON’S CORPORATE CHALLENGE CELEBRATES 2024 WINNERS: HONORING TEAM SPIRIT, CORPORATE WELLNESS AND COMMUNITY IMPACT
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, O.H. (Nov. 19, 2024) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corp. is honored to announce the outstanding success of its Corporate Challenge Program for 2024, proudly sponsored by the County of Summit.

The Corporate Challenge continues to serve as a dynamic platform that fosters a fun and competitive environment, promoting health, fitness, and wellness at every level within the local business community. Designed to support everyone from new participants to experienced athletes, the program provides a seamless addition to corporate wellness efforts.

"Summit County’s businesses consistently support one another and our community,” said Summit County Executive Ilene Shapiro. “Through the Corporate Challenge, they are inspiring their employees to be active and engage in healthy lifestyles, all while building a stronger sense of unity and shared purpose."

This year, the Corporate Challenge saw an impressive 1,325 participants across 33 companies, further establishing it as a cornerstone for promoting a healthy and spirited corporate culture. The awards ceremony, held on Nov. 14, 2024, at the Summit County Chambers, celebrated exceptional achievements and recognized winners in various categories.

Participation Division Winners: 

Scheeser Buckley Mayfield – Division 1 (5 – 44 employees)

Hasenstab Architects – Division 2 (45 – 99 employees)

Bober Markey Fedorovich – Division 3 (100 – 199 employees)

The J.M. Smucker Co. – Division 4 (200 – 649 employees)

National Interstate Insurance Co. – Division 5 (650 – 1,499 employees)

The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co. – Division 6 (1,500+ employees)

Fastest Men’s Corporate Challenge Relay Team Award: Lincoln Electric

Fastest Women’s Corporate Challenge Relay Team Award:

Akron Children's Hospital

Fastest Mixed Corporate Challenge Relay Team Award:

CESO, Inc.

Extra Mile Corporate Challenge for Most Volunteers & Spirit Award:

Summa Health – 63 volunteers, 391 volunteer hours

“We are incredibly proud of the Corporate Challenge’s impact,” said Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “The enthusiastic participation from over 1,000 employees reflects the strong commitment to health and wellness in our community. It’s always inspiring to see businesses come together to compete, support one another, and build a culture of wellness.”

Registration for 2025 opens on Jan. 7 for the Akron Marathon Race Series and the Corporate Challenge Program. To check eligibility for discounted race entry fees, contact your Employee Wellness Coordinator. For questions or additional information, please contact Katie Riley at 330-434-2786 or via email at kriley@akronmarathon.org.

The Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health is organized by the nonprofit Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation whose mission is to promote health and wellness in the community. For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health or the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: AKRON MARATHON HIGHLIGHTS SUCCESS OF 2024 RACE SERIES AND ANNOUNCES SUMMA HEALTH’S RETURN AS PRESENTING SPONSOR FOR AN EXCITING 2025
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, O.H. (Dec. 12, 2024) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation celebrates the remarkable success of its 10th annual Race Series presented by Summa Health, which inspired thousands of runners, walkers, and supporters to embrace health and wellness while making a lasting impact on the Akron community. The 2024 Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health achieved record-breaking milestones:
  • Nearly 12,000 participants celebrated personal victories across the series.
  • 361 race entry scholarships were awarded through the Blue Line Runnership program, ensuring accessibility for all participants.
  • Runners from 45 states and 8 countries contributed to an impressive $6 million economic boost for the greater Akron area.
  • Over $200,000 was raised through the organization’s Blue Line Charity program, benefiting local organizations that make a meaningful difference.
“The 2024 series was an extraordinary celebration of community, perseverance, and impact,” said Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corp. “We are grateful to our runners, volunteers, and sponsors who made this milestone year such a resounding success.” Summa Health Returns as Presenting Sponsor for an Akron Bicentennial Celebration As the Akron Marathon Race Series looks ahead to 2025, it is proud to announce the return of Summa Health as the presenting sponsor of the series. In addition, 2025 promises to be especially exciting as all Race Series events will align with the Akron Bicentennial Celebration, featuring a commemorative series medal designed to honor this historic milestone for the city. “Summa Health is honored to continue our partnership with the Akron Marathon Race Series,” said Dr. Cliff Deveny, president and CEO of Summa Health. “As Akron celebrates its bicentennial, we’re excited to join the community in marking this historic year through these exceptional events that bring us all together in the spirit of health and wellness.” Save the Dates for 2025 The 2025 Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health will feature four signature events as part of the bicentennial festivities. Registration opens on Jan. 7, 2025, at AkronMarathon.org.
  • National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile: June 27-28, 2025
  • Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k: Aug. 9, 2025
  • The Mandel Family Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children’s Hospital: Sept. 26, 2025
  • FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay: Sept. 27, 2025
“2025 will be an special year as we honor Akron’s 200-year legacy alongside the energy and excitement of our series,” added Bitong. “We invite everyone to join us for what promises to be our most memorable season yet."

item.title: AKRON MARATHON AND AKRON BICENTENNIAL COMMISSION LAUNCH WELLNESS CHALLENGE TO CELEBRATE AKRON’S 200TH ANNIVERSARY
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
[et_pb_section fb_built="1" admin_label="section" _builder_version="3.22"][et_pb_row admin_label="row" _builder_version="3.25" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat"][et_pb_column type="4_4" _builder_version="3.25" custom_padding="|||" custom_padding__hover="|||"][et_pb_text admin_label="Text" _builder_version="4.7.7" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat" hover_enabled="0" sticky_enabled="0"]

AKRON, O.H. (Jan. 2, 2025) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation and the Akron Bicentennial Commission are proud to announce the launch of the Akron Bicentennial Wellness Challenge, a collaborative initiative to celebrate Akron’s 200th anniversary through a focus on health and wellness. Beginning Jan. 7, 2025, community members are invited to join the challenge and set a personal goal of completing 200 wellness activities throughout the year. 

What is the Wellness Challenge?  

The Akron Bicentennial Wellness Challenge is an inclusive, yearlong program designed to inspire residents to prioritize health while commemorating Akron’s history. Participants can choose from activities such as walking, running, biking, hiking, swimming, strength training, or any activity that totals at least 15 minutes. The challenge runs from Jan. 7 to Dec. 6, 2025, and those who complete 200 activities will receive a commemorative pin to mark their achievement and celebrate Akron’s milestone.   

“The Wellness Challenge is a wonderful way for Akronites to engage in the Bicentennial while building healthier habits,” said Mark Greer, executive director of Akron 200. “This initiative reflects the spirit of our city—a community that values wellness, togetherness, and progress. As our city celebrates its historic anniversary, participants will be able to chart their own health milestones throughout the year. We’re thrilled to partner with the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation to make this possible.” 

Free and Open to All 

The program is free to participate and is open to everyone in the Akron community, regardless of age or fitness level. Participants can engage in wellness activities that fit their lifestyle and personal goals.  

“This collaboration celebrates the best of Akron: a shared commitment to health and community,” said Anne Bitong, president & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “As a long-standing advocate for wellness through the Akron Marathon Race Series, we’re excited to join forces with the Akron Bicentennial Commission to inspire our community to move, celebrate, and connect with one another.”   

How to Join the Challenge  

Joining is easy! Starting Jan. 7, participants can register by visiting AkronMarathon.org/register. Once registered, they can log their activities, track their progress, and work toward their 200-activity goal. For more details and to access a toolkit with answers to frequently asked questions, visit the registration page.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

item.title: ENCOURAGING THE NEXT GENERATION: AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES OFFERS SAVINGS FOR RUNNERS 24 & UNDER
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, O.H. (Feb. 4, 2025) – The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is excited to announce that young adults aged 24 and under will continue to enjoy introductory pricing across all race events through the registration period, even as general registration prices for the 2025 Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health increased on Feb. 1. This initiative aims to make the Akron Marathon Race Series more inclusive, encouraging young participants to embrace health, fitness, and the joy of crossing the finish line. By offering affordable pricing, the Akron Marathon invites students, young professionals, and first-time participants to join a supportive and inspiring running community. 2025 Race Series Dates:
  • National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile – June 27 & 28, 2025
  • Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k – Aug. 9, 2025
  • FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay – Sept. 27, 2025
“Whether you’re participating in your first event, pushing yourself to a longer distance, or teaming up with friends for the 5-person Team Relay, we want to inspire the next generation of runners,” said Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. To register and learn more about the Akron Marathon Race Series, visit akronmarathon.org.

item.title: AKRON MARATHON CHARITABLE CORPORATION ANNOUNCES NATIONAL INTERSTATE INSURANCE COMPANY AS RETURNING PRESENTING SPONSOR FOR THE 8K & 1 MILE
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON-CANTON REGIONAL FOODBANK NAMED AS OFFICIAL CHARITY

AKRON, O.H. (March 19, 2025) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, organizers of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, proudly welcomes back National Interstate Insurance Company (National Interstate) as the presenting sponsor of the National Interstate 8K & 1 Mile, taking place June 27–28. With just 100 days until race weekend, planning is in full swing.

New this year, the Akron-Canton Regional Foodbank has been named the official charity partner for the event, strengthening the race’s mission to give back to the community. Participants and supporters will have the opportunity to contribute to the Foodbank’s critical efforts in fighting hunger across the region.

National Interstate has been a longstanding supporter of the Akron Marathon Race Series, reinforcing its commitment to health, wellness, and community engagement.

"National Interstate's continued involvement reflects the incredible support from our community’s leading organizations, ensuring the Akron Marathon Race Series continues to inspire and unite our city," said Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. "With dedicated sponsors like National Interstate, Summa Health, FirstEnergy, and The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co., we’re able to create an unforgettable racing experience that celebrates Akron and promotes health, wellness, and community pride."

As part of this year’s initiative, National Interstate is expanding its involvement by using the race as a nationwide employee engagement opportunity, encouraging its team members to participate in whichever way might interest them, whether it be racing, being a race day volunteer, or fundraising to support the official charity partner. 

"We are excited to once again support the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation and the Akron community by sponsoring the 2025 National Interstate 8K & 1 Mile," said Shawn Los, president and COO at National Interstate. "This year, we’re taking it a step further challenging our employees across the country to walk, run, volunteer, and raise funds to fight hunger in our community. "

The National Interstate 8K & 1 Mile is part of Akron’s Bicentennial celebration of events. To register, volunteer, or learn more about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, visit AkronMarathon.org.

# # # 

About the Akron Marathon Race Series  

The Akron Marathon Race Series is organized by the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, a nonprofit group founded in 2002 to provide a world-class marathon and other events that promote health and fitness, stimulate the local economy, galvanize the community, and benefit charitable organizations. The series features race dates in June (National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile) and August (Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k), culminating with the 23rd running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, Team Relay & Kids Fun Run in September. Additional information is available at AkronMarathon.org or by calling (330) 434-2RUN (2786). 

About National Interstate Insurance Company 

An Insurance Experience Built Around You

 

Founded in 1986, National Interstate Insurance Company, is a leading specialty property and casualty insurance company, providing highly innovative insurance solutions and world-class customer service for a variety of commercial transportation industries. Headquartered in Richfield, OH, the company employs over 800 people and has been recognized for years as a “Best Place to Work”, centered around its company values of integrity, transparency, fairness, accountability, empowerment and collaboration.

National Interstate is a member of Great American Insurance Group. The members of Great American Insurance Group are subsidiaries of American Financial Group, Inc. (AFG). AFG’s common stock is listed and traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol AFG.

item.title: AKRON MARATHON CHARITABLE CORPORATION AND FIRSTENERGY LEAD THE CHARGE IN SUSTAINABILITY WITH REUSABLE HYDRAPAK SPEEDCUPS™
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON MARATHON CHARITABLE CORPORATION AND FIRSTENERGY LEAD THE CHARGE IN SUSTAINABILITY WITH REUSABLE HYDRAPAK SPEEDCUPS™

AKRON, O.H. (April 22, 2025) — In celebration of Earth Day, the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, in conjunction with FirstEnergy, is proud to announce a significant stride in sustainability efforts at the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay. For the first time, all race participants will receive a reusable, event-branded HydraPak SpeedCup™ to help reduce waste at fluid stations along the Blue Line racecourse. This initiative represents another step forward in the organization’s ongoing commitment to environmental stewardship.

The introduction of reusable HydraPak SpeedCups™ builds on the tremendous success of last year’s sustainability efforts. The organization diverted 91% of waste from landfills, a 41% increase from the previous year, thanks to the addition of the shoe recycling program and a partnership with Rubber City Reuse, which managed finish line recycling stations.

"We are thrilled to introduce reusable HydraPak SpeedCups™ to this year’s marathon," said Anne Bitong, president & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. "Our goal is to green the Blue Line, and this is one more way we can minimize our environmental impact while encouraging our participants to join us in this effort."

While recyclable paper cups will still be available at fluid stations, the addition of the SpeedCup™ offers participants multiple hydration options. Participants can choose to use the SpeedCup™, their own hydration pack, or the provided paper cups. Fluid stations will be thoughtfully designed to accommodate all three options, with convenient refill stations at the end of each station.

"FirstEnergy is proud to support sustainable initiatives that benefit our community and environment," said Torrence Hinton, president of FirstEnergy Ohio. "Providing reusable SpeedCups™ to thousands of runners is a powerful step forward in reducing race-day waste and fostering a culture of sustainability in Akron."

As FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay organizers continue to champion green initiatives, they encourage participants to take pride in being part of a race that prioritizes environmental responsibility. Together, the community can make a lasting difference by greening the Blue Line, one step at a time.

For more information on sustainability efforts at the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon or to learn how you can get involved, visit akronmarathon.org.

###

About the Akron Marathon Race Series   

The Akron Marathon Race Series is organized by the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, a nonprofit group founded in 2002 to provide a world-class marathon and other events that promote health and fitness, stimulate the local economy, galvanize the community, and benefit charitable organizations. The series features race dates in June (National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile) and August (Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k), culminating with the 23rd running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, Team Relay & Kids Fun Run in September. Additional information is available at AkronMarathon.org or by calling (330) 434-2RUN (2786).  

About FirstEnergy

FirstEnergy is dedicated to integrity, safety, reliability and operational excellence. Its electric distribution companies form one of the nation's largest investor-owned electric systems, serving more than 6 million customers in Ohio, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, West Virginia, Maryland and New York. The company’s transmission subsidiaries operate approximately 24,000 miles of transmission lines that connect the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic regions. Follow FirstEnergy online at firstenergycorp.com and on X, formerly known as Twitter, @FirstEnergyCorp.

item.title: AKRON MARATHON CHARITABLE CORPORATION RECHARGES FIRSTENERGY AKRON MARATHON COURSE FOR 2025
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
[et_pb_section fb_built="1" admin_label="section" _builder_version="3.22"][et_pb_row admin_label="row" _builder_version="3.25" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat"][et_pb_column type="4_4" _builder_version="3.25" custom_padding="|||" custom_padding__hover="|||"][et_pb_text admin_label="Text" _builder_version="4.7.7" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat" hover_enabled="0" sticky_enabled="0"]

AKRON, OH (April 30, 2025) – The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation, organizers of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay, proudly unveil a reimagined course for the 23rd annual event, set for Saturday, September 27. With just 150 days to race day, the updated route offers a vibrant foot tour of Akron’s iconic landmarks while honoring the beloved Blue Line tradition that makes marathon weekend one of the city’s most anticipated events.

The 2025 course features a dynamic downtown start, a new South Main Street finish, and a high-energy Finisher Festival at the newly revitalized Lock 3. Runners can look forward to a smoother, faster experience with reduced elevation in the first half, while preserving Akron’s signature hills for those taking on the challenge of 26.2 miles.

“Listening to our runners is central to everything we do,” said Laura McElrath, VP of operations & race director of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “This year’s course offers a more efficient and fluid first half without losing the character and challenge that make Akron’s marathon a true achievement. Every mile leads to the energy of the Finisher Festival at Lock 3 offering the perfect celebration for runners and spectators alike.”  

Course Preview

Start Line – Akron Art Museum (Mile 0 | 7:00 AM)

Runners will line up along High Street between Mill Street and MLK Boulevard, setting off southbound from the steps of the Akron Art Museum. Flipping the course direction delivers a fresh experience from the very first mile and sets an exciting tone for the miles ahead.

South Akron (Miles 1–3 | 7:05–8:00 AM)

Participants will enjoy a long, steady stretch down High Street, which becomes S. Main Street just before passing Firestone Stadium and the newly renovated athletic fields near the 5K mark.

Firestone Park (Miles 3–5 | 7:15–8:30 AM)

The route winds through Firestone Park, offering shade and charm along tree-lined Firestone Boulevard as runners head toward Brown Street.

The University of Akron (Miles 6–8 | 7:30–9:30 AM)

The first relay exchange takes place at Mile 7 near InfoCision Stadium. Runners will take in the energy of The University of Akron campus before continuing their journey.

All-America Bridge, North Hill & Downtown (Miles 9–12.5 | 7:45–10:50 AM)

Crossing the All-America Bridge into North Hill, Akron’s vibrant international district, runners are greeted by a cultural boost before returning downtown via the Y-Bridge. The course split happens at Mile 12.5: half marathoners veer toward the finish, while full marathoners continue on, and relay teams reach their next exchange zone.

Ohio & Erie Canal Towpath Trail (Miles 13–16 | 8:00–11:30 AM)

A peaceful shift in terrain awaits full marathoners and relay teams as they enter the Towpath Trail. This scenic stretch of crushed limestone runs parallel to the historic canal, offering a flat, steady rhythm ahead of the hills to come.

Sand Run Metro Park (Miles 17–19 | 8:30 AM–12:00 PM)

The trail transitions to the natural serenity of Sand Run Metro Park. Runners will find shade, rolling hills, and the third relay exchange amid one of Akron’s most scenic green spaces.

West Akron (Miles 20–23 | 8:40 AM–1:25 PM)

Crowds and community pride power runners through the West Akron neighborhoods, known for Blue Line block parties and spirited encouragement. This stretch includes the final relay exchange, Garman Hill, and views of Stan Hywet Hall & Gardens, providing inspiration as runners push toward the final stretch.

Return to Downtown (Miles 24–26.2 | 9:15 AM–1:30 PM)

The final miles down Portage Path through Highland Square and West Market Street before the dramatic finish down South Main Street. The energy here is palpable, fueled by spectators, music, and the thrill of the finish line ahead.

The Finish (8:00 AM-2:00 PM)

Runners will cross the finish line near the Akron Civic Theatre and step directly into celebration at the FirstEnergy Finisher Festival in Lock 3. The newly reimagined venue will be buzzing with excitement showcasing food trucks and live music welcoming runners and spectators alike.

A Recharged Experience

The redesigned 2025 course delivers a brand-new perspective for returning participants and a warm welcome to first-timers, all while celebrating Akron’s Bicentennial. With a blend of fresh scenery, iconic landmarks, and the unmistakable community spirit Akron is known for, the 23rd annual event promises an unforgettable race weekend and a once-in-a-lifetime moment in the city’s history.

Registration is open for all events in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. Runners are encouraged to sign up early to secure their spot in one of Ohio’s premier racing experiences. Price increases are set for May 1, July 1, and August 15. Visit AkronMarathon.org and follow @AkronMarathon on social media for the latest updates.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

All-America Bridge, North Hill & Downtown (Miles 9–12.5 | 7:45–10:50 AM)

Crossing the All-America Bridge into North Hill, Akron’s vibrant international district, runners are greeted by a cultural boost before returning downtown via the Y-Bridge. The course split happens at Mile 12.5: half marathoners veer toward the finish, while full marathoners continue on, and relay teams reach their next exchange zone.

Ohio & Erie Canal Towpath Trail (Miles 13–16 | 8:00–11:30 AM)

A peaceful shift in terrain awaits full marathoners and relay teams as they enter the Towpath Trail. This scenic stretch of crushed limestone runs parallel to the historic canal, offering a flat, steady rhythm ahead of the hills to come.

Sand Run Metro Park (Miles 17–19 | 8:30 AM–12:00 PM)

The trail transitions to the natural serenity of Sand Run Metro Park. Runners will find shade, rolling hills, and the third relay exchange amid one of Akron’s most scenic green spaces.

West Akron (Miles 20–23 | 8:40 AM–1:25 PM)

Crowds and community pride power runners through the West Akron neighborhoods, known for Blue Line block parties and spirited encouragement. This stretch includes the final relay exchange, Garman Hill, and views of Stan Hywet Hall & Gardens, providing inspiration as runners push toward the final stretch.

Return to Downtown (Miles 24–26.2 | 9:15 AM–1:30 PM)

The final miles down Portage Path through Highland Square and West Market Street before the dramatic finish down South Main Street. The energy here is palpable, fueled by spectators, music, and the thrill of the finish line ahead.

The Finish (8:00 AM-2:00 PM)

Runners will cross the finish line near the Akron Civic Theatre and step directly into celebration at the FirstEnergy Finisher Festival in Lock 3. The newly reimagined venue will be buzzing with excitement showcasing food trucks and live music welcoming runners and spectators alike.

A Recharged Experience

The redesigned 2025 course delivers a brand-new perspective for returning participants and a warm welcome to first-timers, all while celebrating Akron’s Bicentennial. With a blend of fresh scenery, iconic landmarks, and the unmistakable community spirit Akron is known for, the 23rd annual event promises an unforgettable race weekend and a once-in-a-lifetime moment in the city’s history.

Registration is open for all events in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. Runners are encouraged to sign up early to secure their spot in one of Ohio’s premier racing experiences. Price increases are set for May 1, July 1, and August 15. Visit AkronMarathon.org and follow @AkronMarathon on social media for the latest updates.

item.title: OLYMPIAN BUTCH REYNOLDS NAMED 2025 AKRON MARATHON AMBASSADOR AWARD RECIPIENT
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, OH (June 4, 2025) – The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is proud to announce that Olympic gold medalist and Akron native Butch Reynolds has been selected as the 2025 Ambassador Award recipient. This prestigious honor will be presented during the 23rd annual FirstEnergy Akron Marathon weekend as the organization celebrates not only the power of running, but also Akron’s Bicentennial and those who have helped shape its legacy. Reynolds, who is the subject of the award-winning ESPN 30 for 30 Documentary "False Positive,” continues to inspire through his athletic achievements and unwavering commitment to the community. Reynolds, a world-record holder, gold medalist in the 4x400 relay, and silver medalist in the 400 meters at the 1988 Seoul Olympics, is celebrated both for his elite athletic accomplishments and his commitment to empowering youth through health, wellness, and education. His lasting impact as a mentor and community advocate has made him an icon in Akron and beyond. “Reynolds is more than a champion on the track, he’s a champion for the people of Akron,” said Jeannine Marks, race founder and board chair of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “In this historic year for our city, we are thrilled to honor someone whose personal and professional journey embodies the spirit, resilience, and pride of Akron.” The Ambassador Award is presented annually to an individual who has made significant contributions and lasting impact on the sport of running. This award honors those who inspire others to run through their commitment and enthusiasm. Reynolds will be honored at the annual Akron Marathon Kickoff Event & VIP Party on Wednesday, Sept. 24. The invitation-only celebration will bring together community leaders, sponsors, and supporters. “I was at the inaugural Kids Fun Run, and I’m honored to come back home to Akron for this special weekend,” said Reynolds. “It means so much to be recognized by my hometown and to once again help promote health and wellness to our youth, especially during Akron’s Bicentennial. I can’t wait to celebrate with this amazing community.” In addition to the VIP reception, Reynolds will be on-site throughout marathon weekend: Friday, Sept. 26
  • Meet fans at the Health & Fitness Expo presented by the Akron Area YMCA at the John S. Knight Center
  • Serve as the honorary starter for The Mandel Family Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children’s Hospital
Saturday, Sept. 27
  • Kick off the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay and participate in the post-race awards ceremonies
This year’s event promises to be one of the most memorable yet, with plenty to celebrate. We look forward to honoring Reynolds for his lasting legacy, commemorating Akron’s historic Bicentennial, unveiling a reimagined racecourse, and debuting an all-new finish line experience at Lock 3. It’s a milestone year that blends tradition with transformation, and the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation looks forward to celebrating alongside the community every step of the way. To register and learn more about the Akron Marathon Race Series, visit akronmarathon.org.

item.title: AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES OPENS WITH THOUSANDS PARTICIPATING IN NATIONAL INTERSTATE 8K & 1 MILE
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
