AKRON, O.H. (June 28, 2025) — The National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile drew over 2,000 participants, spanning all ages from infants in the stroller division up to 81 years old. This event marked the beginning of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, taking place on Fri., June 27, 2025, and Sat., June 28, 2025. This year’s event also took on added significance as it coincided with Akron’s Bicentennial celebration, making it a truly special moment to honor the city’s legacy. “This year’s event was especially meaningful as we celebrated not only our participants, volunteers, and sponsors, but also Akron’s Bicentennial,” said Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “Bringing people together through movement and community pride is at the core of our mission, and it was inspiring to see that come to life across every mile.”  Kyle Stober from Mogadore secured the 8k victory in the men's division of the National Interstate 8k, while Jo Line from Akron triumphed in the women's division. Nick Marino from Stow and Hannah Long from Akron dominated in the 1 Mile race.  In the non-binary category, Eva Nel Brettrager from Brunswick claimed first place in the 1 Mile, continuing to highlight the Akron Marathon’s ongoing commitment to inclusivity and representation.  “As presenting sponsor of the Akron Marathon Race Series, Summa Health is proud to support an event that encourages healthy lifestyles and brings our community together,” said Cliff Deveny, M.D., president and CEO of Summa Health. “Seeing participants of all backgrounds and abilities come together on race day is a powerful reminder of what it means to build a stronger, healthier community.” The course for the National Interstate 8k & 1 Mile began by highlighting The University of Akron's campus, offering a unique foot tour of downtown Akron, and ended with a memorable finisher’s festival featuring food trucks, live music, and more. “National Interstate is proud to renew our sponsorship of the 8k & 1 Mile events as part of the Akron Marathon Race Series,” said Shawn Los, president and chief operating officer at National Interstate Insurance Company. “This event offers a great opportunity to encourage health and wellness, both within our company and across the community. item.title: GOODYEAR HALF MARATHON & 10K WRAPS WITH VICTORIES AND BLIMP MILESTONE
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, OH (Aug. 9, 2025) — Nearly 2,400 athletes came together to celebrate Akron’s Bicentennial at Goodyear’s Akron Proving Grounds Test Track for the second event in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health on Sat., Aug. 9, 2025, beginning at 6:30 a.m.

“On behalf of the Akron Marathon team, we’re grateful to Goodyear and our community for helping us create another successful race day,” said Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “It was an honor to celebrate two major milestones—the 100th anniversary of the Goodyear Blimp and Akron’s Bicentennial—with runners, volunteers and supporters.”

The Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k welcomed participants from ages 6 to 81, from 23 states and 7 countries. Just as the Goodyear Blimp has become a recognizable symbol over the past century, this race continues to grow as a meaningful tradition within Akron.

Riley Worl and defending women’s champion Andrea Klima were the Goodyear Half Marathon men’s and women’s division winners, finishing at 1:11:24 and 1:21:05, with Klima bettering her time by two seconds from last year. The men’s 10k winner, Joseph Redle, finished with a time of 32:42, and the women’s 10k winner, Ashton Swinford, finished with a time of 36:05.

In the non-binary category, Fern Nichols from Akron claimed first place in the Half Marathon, and Vanessa Rivera from Columbus excelled in the 10k, reflecting our ongoing commitment to inclusivity.

“We’re proud to sponsor an event that showcases the spirit of Akron through stories of perseverance, courage and wellness,” said Doug Grassian, vice president, global external communications, social media and partnerships of The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company and Akron Marathon board member. “It’s truly meaningful to see athletes, volunteers, families and fans all together to celebrate achievement and community.”

item.title: FIRSTENERGY AKRON MARATHON ANNOUNCES 2025 SCHEDULE OF EVENTS, BICENTENNIAL CELEBRATION, AND COURSE ENHANCEMENTS FOR SEPT. 26-27, 2025
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded: AKRON, O.H. (Sept. 4, 2025) – The FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay is proud to welcome participants to its 23rd annual event on Sept. 26–27, 2025. This milestone year coincides with Akron’s Bicentennial and features a recharged course, a new South Main Street finish, and the FirstEnergy Finisher Festival at the renovated Lock 3. As part of the Bicentennial celebration, participant shirts, race bibs, and medals will feature the Akron Bicentennial logo, creating a special keepsake from this milestone year. Blending exciting updates with the spirit of the Blue Line, the event celebrates every finisher and Akron’s 200-year legacy. Olympic gold medalist and Akron’s own Butch Reynolds will also be on hand throughout race weekend, appearing at the Health & Fitness Expo and helping to kick off both the Kids Fun Run and Marathon as part of the Bicentennial celebration. Race weekend has become one of Akron’s signature community events, and in this Bicentennial year, organizers invite everyone to run, walk, cheer, or volunteer to help create the energy and pride that make the celebration unforgettable. Health & Fitness Expo presented by the Akron Area YMCA Kicks Off Race Weekend The festivities begin on Friday, Sept. 26, with the Health and Fitness Expo presented by the Akron Area YMCA at the John S. Knight Center, located at 77 E. Mill St, Akron. The Expo, open from 11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., is free and open to the public. It features race packet pickup, where participants can collect their race bib, shirt, and other essential items before the big day. New this year, the Expo will showcase the RunAkron collaborative mural, sponsored by The Fuchs and Kranz Family Foundations, inviting attendees to make their mark on a community art piece that will later be displayed at the FirstEnergy Finisher Festival and permanently installed at Akron Marathon headquarters. Attendees can also explore the Ready, Set, PR Zone, designed to help runners look and feel their best with complimentary experiences like hair braiding, custom shoe charms, glitter freckles, and inspirational temporary tattoos. Additional highlights include the Akron Marathon Official Merchandise Store presented by Fleet Feet, the Runner’s Lounge with NormaTec boots and massages, and the spectator sign-making station, giving fans the chance to create personalized signs to cheer on participants. The Mandel Family Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children’s Hospital Promises Family Fun Also on Friday, families are invited to The Mandel Family Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children's Hospital. This free event starts at 214 W. Bowery St and finishes at Lock 3, 200 S. Main St. The registration tent opens at 5:00 p.m., with the run kicking off at 6:00 p.m. About 1,000 children are expected to participate in this fun-filled event, where kids are encouraged to run, walk, hop, skip, and jump their way to the finish line. Main Event: FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay The main event takes place on Saturday, Sept. 27, beginning with the Opening Ceremony at 6:00 a.m. The FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay starts at 7:00 a.m. at the Akron Art Museum, 1 S. High St., and finishes at Lock 3, 200 S. Main St. This year’s recharged course, first introduced in April, keeps the iconic downtown start but features a refreshed first nine miles and updated relay-leg distances. Runners will still experience the same great Akron neighborhoods and landmarks, along with entertainment and block parties at every mile. Thanks to the support of FirstEnergy, participants will receive a HydraPak SpeedCup to use at refill stations along the course as part of enhanced sustainability efforts that reduce waste while keeping runners hydrated. After crossing the Blue Line finish, participants are invited to celebrate at the all-new FirstEnergy Finisher Festival at the revitalized Lock 3, featuring live music, food trucks, and an energized community atmosphere. Be Part of the Energy: Volunteer for Race Weekend Help us celebrate Akron’s Bicentennial and make the 23rd annual FirstEnergy Akron Marathon Race Weekend unforgettable! From welcoming runners and managing fluid stations to cheering along the Blue Line, there are countless ways to get involved. Volunteers receive a free event t-shirt, a commemorative pin, and the chance to be part of one of Akron’s most cherished traditions. Sign up today at https://www.akronmarathon.org/volunteer/ and add your energy to race weekend! Schedule of Events Friday, Sept. 26 Health & Fitness Expo presented by the Akron Area YMCA: John S. Knight Center, 77 E. Mill St, Akron 11:00 a.m. – Doors Open 8:00 p.m. – Doors Close The Mandel Family Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children’s Hospital: Start at 214 W. Bowery St, Finish at Lock 3, 200 S. Main St. 5:00 p.m. – Registration Tent / Bib Pickup Opens 6:00 p.m. – Race Start 6:45 p.m. – Course Closes 7:30 p.m. – Venue Closes Saturday, Sept. 27 FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay: Start at Akron Art Museum, 1 S. High St, Akron, Finish at Lock 3, 200 S. Main St. 6:00 a.m. – Opening Ceremony 6:59 a.m. – Wheelchair Division & Push Team Start 7:00 a.m. – Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay Start 7:35 a.m. – FirstEnergy Finisher Festival Opens 8:50 a.m. – Half Marathon Overall Awards 10:45 a.m. – Marathon Overall Awards 1:45 p.m. – Course Closes 2:00 p.m. – Finisher Festival Closes “We are grateful to Summa Health as presenting sponsor of our Race Series and to FirstEnergy for their longstanding support of marathon weekend,” said Anne Bitong, president & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “In this special Bicentennial year, their commitment helps us celebrate every runner crossing the Blue Line and Akron’s 200-year legacy, showcasing the energy behind every step and the community behind every mile.” For more information and to register to run, walk, cheer, or volunteer, visit www.akronmarathon.org or follow us on social media @AkronMarathon. Online registration closes on Sunday, Sept. 21 for all events.

item.title: BLUE LINERS CROSS THE FINISH LINE AS AKRON MARKS 200 YEARS AT THE 23RD FIRSTENERGY AKRON MARATHON
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, O.H. (Sept. 27, 2025) — Thousands of runners and spectators filled the streets of Akron this weekend for the 23rd running of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay, a tradition that coincided this year with the city’s historic bicentennial celebration. The milestone event brought the community together as athletes, families, and fans gathered to honor 200 years of Akron alongside a world-class race experience. Headlining the marathon was Aaron Davidson from Flagstaff, AZ, who defended his title after winning last year with a time of 2:25:30. This year, he beat his previous time and claimed victory again, finishing in 2:18:59. In the women’s division, Ashton Swinford of Hudson secured the win, finishing with a strong time of 2:51:24. “Celebrating Akron’s Bicentennial makes this year’s marathon even more meaningful,” said Anne Bitong, president & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “The energy of the community, the dedication of our runners, and the support of our partners truly showcase what makes Akron special.” The FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay welcomed athletes from 36 U.S. states and 4 countries, adding to the marathon’s reputation as one of the premier running events in the Midwest. In the half marathon, Eric Westog of Chelsea, MI, claimed the men’s title in 1:07:54, while Alyssa Thomas of North Royalton won the women’s division in 1:15:25, marking her third victory and second consecutive win in the event. In the non-binary category, Noah Chavez from Cleveland claimed first place in the marathon, reflecting our ongoing commitment to inclusivity.  The city came alive as runners followed the recharged course through Akron, beginning at the Akron Art Museum and finishing at the newly renovated Lock 3. The updated route refreshed the first half of the course while keeping runners immersed in the city’s iconic neighborhoods, with supporters lining the Blue Line to cheer athletes on every step of the way. “In Akron’s 200th year, the Blue Line was more energized than ever—a celebration of everything that makes our city so exceptional,” said Torrence Hinton, President – Ohio for FirstEnergy. “Supporting this event allows us to honor the collective energy and character that define our city year after year. It’s an inspiring reminder of how far we’ve come—and how much farther we’ll go together.” This year’s Akron Marathon Race Series Corporate Challenge, presented by the County of Summit, saw an incredible turnout with 1,806 participants from 26 organizations. Final standings for the Corporate Challenge will be announced later this fall. The weekend festivities kicked off with Friday’s Mandel Family Kids Fun Run presented by Akron Children’s. Nearly 1,000 young runners, ages 12 and under, had their moment to shine as they raced the one-mile course to cross the same finish line as the marathoners, greeted by cheering crowds and family members. item.title: AKRON MARATHON CHARITABLE CORPORATION CELEBRATES CORPORATE CHALLENGE 2025 WINNERS
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole

AKRON, O.H. (Nov. 20, 2025) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is honored to announce the success of its Corporate Challenge Program, sponsored by the County of Summit.    The Corporate Challenge has proven to be a catalyst for a fun and competitive environment, promoting health, fitness, and wellness at every level in the local business community. From couch to 8k, to first-time marathoners, this challenge provides a turnkey program that seamlessly integrates into corporate wellness initiatives.  “Summit County businesses have once again rallied around the marathon tradition, embracing friendly competition and a focus on health and wellness,” said Ilene Shapiro, Summit County Executive. “The Corporate Challenge showcases the teamwork and community pride that make Summit County such a special place to live and work.” 

More than 1,700 runners across 26 companies participated in the Corporate Challenge this racing season, turning it into a platform for a healthy and vibrant corporate culture. The awards ceremony took place on Nov. 19, 2025, at the Summit County Chambers, and honored outstanding achievements and celebrated the winners in various categories. 

Participation Division Winners:  

Division 1 (5 - 44 Employees) – Scheeser Buckley Mayfield 

Division 2 (45 - 99 Employees) – Hasenstab Architects 

Division 3 (100 - 199 Employees) – Wright Tool  

Division 4 (200 - 649 Employees) – Parker Meggitt 

Division 5 (650 - 1,499 Employees) – National Interstate Insurance 

Division 6 (1,500+ Employees) – The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company

Summa Health – 32 Social Media Posts

FirstEnergy – Raised $100,000 for the Akron-Canton Regional Foodbank 

“It’s been incredible to watch the Corporate Challenge evolve into such a meaningful part of our race series,” said Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “The way local businesses rally together embodies everything the Blue Line stands for, including wellness, teamwork, and community.”  

Looking to participate in 2026? Registration for the Akron Marathon Race Series opens in January. To check eligibility for discounted race entry fees, contact your Employee Wellness Coordinator. For questions or additional information, please contact Sammi Riggs at (330) 434 – 2786 or via email at sriggs@akronmarathon.org.

item.title: ACME FRESH MARKET FOUNDATION NAMED PRESENTING SPONSOR OF THE 8K & 1 MILE, KICKING OFF THE AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, O.H. (Dec. 30, 2025) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation announces that the Acme Fresh Market Foundation is the presenting sponsor of the 2026 8k & 1 Mile, the kickoff race of the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. The Foundation succeeds National Interstate Insurance Company beginning in 2026, elevating a partnership that has supported Akron’s running community since the Marathon’s inception.

For more than two decades, Acme Fresh Market has helped fuel the Akron Marathon experience, providing runners with water, bananas, and recovery snacks throughout race weekend. With a 125-year legacy of feeding and supporting families across Northeast Ohio, the expanded partnership reflects a shared commitment to health, wellness, and community.

“The Akron Marathon Race Series is one of our region’s most inspiring celebrations of health, community, and togetherness,” said Katie Swartz, Vice President of Marketing, Acme Fresh Market. “We are honored to deepen our support as presenting sponsor of the 8k & 1 Mile and look forward to helping families across Northeast Ohio start their race season with energy, excitement, and fun.”

As part of this enhanced partnership, the 8k & 1 Mile will return to InfoCision Stadium, offering participants a memorable on-field finish and a post-race celebration inside the stadium, complete with fresh snacks and a festive atmosphere. The event will also debut the Acme Fresh Family 1 Mile, designed to inspire runners, walkers, and families, including kids and strollers, to take part together. Both events, the 8k & 1 Mile are scheduled for Saturday, June 27, 2026.

“We are grateful to expand our partnership with the Acme Fresh Market Foundation,” said Anne Bitong, president & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “Their dedication to strengthening families and improving community well-being makes them a natural partner as we launch the 2026 Race Series with a shared commitment to health, wellness, and community connection.”

The 8k & 1 Mile presented by the Acme Fresh Market Foundation anchors the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, followed by the Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k on August 8 and culminating with the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay in the fall on September 26.

Registration for all 2026 Akron Marathon Race Series events opens Jan. 7, 2026, at AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: NEARLY 1,700 PARTICIPANTS KICK OFF 2026 AKRON MARATHON RACE SERIES AT ACME FRESH MARKET FOUNDATION 8K & 1 MILE
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, O.H. (June 27, 2026) — 1,700 participants gathered Saturday for the Acme Fresh Market Foundation 8k & 1 Mile, launching the 2026 Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. The event brought together runners, walkers and families of all ages and abilities, including the debut of the new Family 1 Mile, for a morning celebrating movement, health and community.

“Every year, the first event of the Akron Marathon Race Series reminds us why this community is so special,” said Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “The excitement from our participants, volunteers and supporters creates an incredible atmosphere and sets the tone for an unforgettable race season ahead.” 

The 8k welcomed a strong field of athletes, with Joseph Redle from Fairlawn, OH earning the men’s division victory and Andrea Klima from Independence, OH claiming the women’s division title and setting a new event record. 

In the 1 Mile event, Noah Bernarding of Cochranton, PA finished first in the men's race, while returning champion Hannah Long of Akron, OH successfully defended her women's title.

"As presenting sponsor of the Akron Marathon Race Series, Summa Health is proud to support events that inspire people of all ages to prioritize their health and well-being," said Daryl Tol, acting president and CEO of Summa Health. "Today’s event is a great example of how movement brings people together and strengthens our community."

This year’s event returned to InfoCision Stadium, where participants celebrated an on-field finish and post-race festivities. New this year, the Family 1 Mile and Kids Zone provided additional opportunities for families to participate together and enjoy an active day in Akron.

“The Acme Fresh Market Foundation was excited to take on this expanded partnership in 2026 and support the Akron Marathon Race Series in an even more meaningful way,” said Katie Swartz, Vice President of Marketing, the Acme Fresh Market. “For more than two decades, we have been proud to support the marathon experience and help fuel runners throughout race weekend, and it’s incredibly rewarding to continue that tradition as families and participants came together to kick off the race season.”

The winners included: 

Men’s 8k: 

  1. JOSEPH REDLE, FAIRLAWN, OH, 25:43

  1. JAKE SUTTELL, AKRON, OH, 26:21

  1. KYLE STOBER, MOGADORE, OH, 26:36

Women’s 8k:

Men’s Masters 8k:

  1. DAVID BALTHIS, CANTON, OH, 32:51

Women’s Masters 8k:  

  1. ALISSA KOLARIK, WADSWORTH, OH, 34:22

  1. TERESA FERGUSON, AKRON, OH, 34:37

  1. ERICA DROST, ROCKY RIVER, OH, 36:02

Non-Binary 8k: 

  1. MATTHEW NYCE, MAYFIELD HEIGHTS, OH, 40:48

  1. SPENCER BAKER, AKRON, OH, 50:40

Men’s 1 Mile:  

  1. NOAH BERNARDING, COCHRANTON, PA, 4:30

  1. NATE BERTMAN, CHAGRIN FALLS, OH, 4:52

  1. CHARLES NOVAK, CUYAHOGA FALLS, OH, 5:02

 

Women’s 1 Mile:  

  1. HANNAH LONG, AKRON, OH, 5:02

  1. KARSYN SPEARS, CRANBERRY TWP, PA, 5:10

  1. KELLY SCULLY, CUYAHOGA FALLS, OH, 5:35

 

Men’s Masters 1 Mile:  

  1. MATTHEW STUDY, NORTHFIELD, OH, 6:06

  1. FRANK ZGRABIK, NORTHFIELD, OH, 6:15

  1. ARIEL UBBEN, AKRON, OH, 6:19

 

Women’s Masters 1 Mile: 

  1. LAURA PAWAR, MEDINA, OH, 6:11

  1. MEGAN VARGA, CUYAHOGA FALLS, OH, 7:10

  1. DIXA DHITAL, HUDSON, OH, 7:16

The 2026 Akron Marathon Race Series continues with the Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k on Aug. 8, followed by the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon & Team Relay on Sept. 26. Registration and volunteer opportunities for both events are available at AkronMarathon.org.

For more information about the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health, please visit AkronMarathon.org.

item.title: SEQUOIA FINANCIAL GROUP TO BE PRESENTING SPONSOR OF THE FIRSTENERGY AKRON MARATHON VIP PARTY
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
AKRON, OHIO (July 8, 2026) — The Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation is proud to announce that Sequoia Financial Group has partnered with organizers to be the presenting sponsor of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon VIP Party, the official kickoff celebration for the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon Weekend.

The FirstEnergy Akron Marathon VIP Party presented by Sequoia Financial Group will be held on Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026. The invitation-only event celebrates the partnerships and people that help make the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon Weekend possible while building excitement for race weekend.

“Marathon weekend celebrates months of preparation and personal commitment,” said Anne Bitong, president & CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. “We are thrilled to welcome Sequoia Financial Group as the presenting sponsor of the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon VIP Party. Sequoia’s commitment to helping individuals and families plan for the future reflects the same values of preparation, perseverance, and long-term impact that inspire our participants and the Akron Marathon community.”

As presenting sponsor, Sequoia Financial Group will help welcome community leaders, sponsors, volunteers, and supporters to an evening celebrating the partnerships that make the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon Weekend possible. The partnership reflects Sequoia’s commitment to investing in the Akron community, with team members and clients actively participating in Akron Marathon events as runners, volunteers, and champions of healthy, connected communities.

“At Sequoia Financial Group, we believe strong communities are built through meaningful relationships and long-term investments,” said Tom Haught, chairman & CEO. “The FirstEnergy Akron Marathon Weekend is one of Akron’s most celebrated traditions, bringing together thousands of participants, volunteers, and supporters. We are honored to support the VIP Party and celebrate the partnerships that help make this event possible.”

Each year, the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon Weekend welcomes thousands of participants and spectators while generating significant economic activity throughout Greater Akron. The event showcases the region, inspires healthy lifestyles, and highlights the collaborative spirit that has defined the Akron Marathon for more than two decades.

item.title: GOODYEAR HALF MARATHON & 10K CELEBRATES FAST FINISHES AND CHAMPIONSHIP PERFORMANCES
item.dc:creator: LaurenToole
item.content:encoded:
[et_pb_section fb_built="1" admin_label="section" _builder_version="4.16" global_colors_info="{}"][et_pb_row admin_label="row" _builder_version="4.16" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat" global_colors_info="{}"][et_pb_column type="4_4" _builder_version="4.16" custom_padding="|||" global_colors_info="{}" custom_padding__hover="|||"][et_pb_text admin_label="Text" _builder_version="4.27.6" background_size="initial" background_position="top_left" background_repeat="repeat" hover_enabled="0" global_colors_info="{}" sticky_enabled="0"]

AKRON, OH (Aug. 8, 2026) — Participants gathered Saturday, Aug. 8 for the Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k, the second event in the Akron Marathon Race Series presented by Summa Health. The event featured a sold-out Half Marathon, returning champions, participants ages 7 to 82, and runners representing 23 states and five countries, creating an exciting morning at Goodyear Headquarters.

"Every race day is a celebration of the people who make this event possible," said Anne Bitong, president and CEO of the Akron Marathon Charitable Corporation. "We're grateful to Goodyear, Summa Health, the City of Akron, our many partners, volunteers and participants for creating another incredible race experience. From first-time participants to returning champions, race day reminds us that when our community comes together, everyone moves forward."

The race showcased impressive performances across both race distances, with elite competition, personal bests, first-time finishers and thousands for finish line celebrations.

"As presenting sponsor of the Akron Marathon Race Series, Summa Health is proud to support events that encourage people to stay active and invest in their health," said Daryl Tol, acting president and CEO of Summa Health. "The Goodyear Half Marathon & 10k is an inspiring reminder that every mile, every finish line and every personal achievement contribute to a healthier, stronger community. We're honored to celebrate the dedication of every participant and look forward to continuing that momentum as we complete the series in September."

In the Half Marathon, three-time champion Andrea Klima claimed the women's overall title with a time of 1:19:45, improving on her winning time each year. Zavier Medina finished first among the men with a time of 1:12:59.

Josh Maple placed second in the men’s masters Half Marathon division with a time of 1:30:56, while his daughter, Sarah Maple, finished second in the women’s Half Marathon with a time of 1:25:25.

Returning 10k champion Joseph Redle secured the men's overall title with a time of 32:03, improving on his 2025 winning time of 32:42. Three-time champion Ashton Swinford claimed the women’s 10k title with a time of 36:01, continuing her streak of improving her winning time each year.

“We're proud to welcome participants to the Goodyear Proving Grounds each year for a day that inspires people to challenge themselves and celebrate their accomplishments," said Doug Grassian, vice president, global external communications, social media and partnerships for The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company and Akron Marathon board member. "Whether someone is participating, volunteering or cheering from the sidelines, this event creates lasting connections and highlights what can be achieved when a community comes together."

The day’s winners included: 

HALF MARATHON FINAL RESULTS:

MALE OVERALL – 

1. Zavier Medina, North Canton, 1:12:59

2. Jake Suttell, Akron, 1:13:05

3. Grant Powers, Westlake, 1:13:42

FEMALE OVERALL –

1. Andrea Klima, Independence, 1:19:45

2. Sarah Maple, Fort Wayne, IN, 1:25:25

3. Caroline Bialke, Wadsworth, 1:25:31

MASTERS MALE –

1. Ryan McCartney, Cleveland, 1:18:47

2. Josh Maple, Fort Wayne, IN, 1:30:56

3. Harsha Mudrakola, Akron, 1:31:10

MASTERS FEMALE –

1. Alissa Kolarik, Wadsworth, 1:28:58

2. Teresa Ferguson, Akron, 1:32:41

3. Danelle Villers, Copley, 1:34:17

NON-BINARY –

1. Matthew Nyce, Mayfield Heights, 1:58:43 

10K FINAL RESULTS:

MALE OVERALL –

1. Joseph Redle, Fairlawn, 32:03

2. Romagn Wingate, Creston, 34:44

3. Justin Zapotoczny, Navarre, 35:34

FEMALE OVERALL –

1. Ashton Swinford, Hudson, 36:01

2. Beth Reppermund, Brecksville, 42:17

3. KC Woodford, Akron, 42:49

MASTERS MALE –

1. Jed Koops, Shaker Heights, 39:30

2. Joe Sauerbrey, Thomasville, NC, 41:36

3. Jeff Loofboro, Kent, OH, 42:52

MASTERS FEMALE –

1. Rachel Laymon, Akron, 46:21

2. Maria Prinzo, Barberton, 47:55

3. Ashley Carroll, Richfield, 49:13

NON-BINARY –

1. Manny Perez, Austintown, 53:50

2. Vanessa Rivera, Columbus, 1:04:46

3. Katelyn Gress, Akron OH, 1:42:19

For race registration and volunteer opportunities for the final race series event, visit AkronMarathon.org. The culminating event, the 24th annual FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, & Team Relay, will take place on Sept. 26, 2026.
